title.zh: 卷十六 志第六 律曆上
title.en: Volume 16 Treatises 6: Rhythm and the Calendar Part One
title.raw: 卷十六 志第六 律曆上 Volume 16 Treatises 6: Rhythm and the Calendar Part One

sentences.zh: 卷一十六 志第六

translations.literal: Volume 16, Treatise 6.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 16, Treatise Six.

sentences.zh: 律曆志上

translations.literal: Treatise on Pitch Standards and the Calendar, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on the Pitch Pipes and the Calendar, Part One

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「形而上者謂之道，形而下者謂之器。

translations.literal: The "Book of Changes" says: "What is above form is called the Way; what is below form is called the vessel."
translations.idiomatic: The "Book of Changes" distinguishes the Way, which transcends concrete form, from "vessels"—the patterned instruments that embody it.

sentences.zh: 」夫神道廣大，妙本於陰陽；

translations.literal: The spirit-like Way is vast; its subtle root lies in yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: That numinous Way is boundless, yet its subtle foundation is still the interplay of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 形器精微，義先於律呂。

translations.literal: Form and vessels are minute and fine; their meaning is anchored first in the pitch pipes and notes.
translations.idiomatic: Concrete forms and ritual implements are refined down to the smallest detail, and their meaning begins with the regulation of pitch pipes and scale degrees.

sentences.zh: 聖人觀四時之變，刻玉紀其盈虛，察五行之聲，鑄金均其清濁，所以遂八風而宣九德，和大樂而成政道。

translations.literal: The sages observed the transformations of the four seasons, carved jade to record waxing and waning, and examined the tones of the five phases, casting metal to balance clear and muddy sounds; thereby they followed the eight winds, spread the nine powers of virtue, harmonized great music, and completed the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: By watching the turning seasons they cut jade tallies for fullness and decline; by listening to the five phases in sound they cast bronze to balance bright and dull registers—so the eight winds could be brought into accord, the nine virtues proclaimed, court music perfected, and governance given its proper tone.

sentences.zh: 然金質從革，侈弇無方；

translations.literal: Yet metal's substance follows the hide; its flare and constriction admit no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze, however, yields to the worker's hand—its bore widens or narrows without a single fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 竹體圓虛，修短利制。

translations.literal: Bamboo is round and hollow; length and shortness lend themselves to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo tubes are naturally round and hollow, so their length can be cut to precise measure.

sentences.zh: 是以神瞽作律，用寫鐘聲，乃紀之以三，平之以六，成於十二，天之道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the blind music masters devised the pitch pipes to capture the bell's voice, recording it in threes, leveling it in sixes, completing it in twelve—this is the pattern of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The blind masters therefore framed the pipes to write down the Yellow Bell's note: they grouped it in threes, evened it in sixes, and finished the cycle at twelve pipes—the same numerology Heaven itself uses.

sentences.zh: 又葉時日於晷度，效地氣于灰管，故陰陽和則景至，律氣應則灰飛。

translations.literal: They also aligned the seasons and days with the gnomon's shadow and tested earth's qi in ash-filled tubes; thus when yin and yang are in harmony the shadow arrives true, and when the pipe's qi responds the ash flies.
translations.idiomatic: They matched the calendar to gnomon readings and read the breath of the soil in thermoscopic tubes, so harmony of yin and yang showed in the solstitial shadow, while the monthly pipe's breath showed when the light ash sprang.

sentences.zh: 灰飛律通，吹而命之，則天地之中聲也。

translations.literal: When the ash flies and the pitch responds, blowing it defines the mid-tone of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ash leaps and the pipe answers, a single sustained breath names the central tone that stands between Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 故可以範圍百度，化成萬品，則《虞書》所謂「葉時月正日，同律度量衡」者也。

translations.literal: Therefore it can compass the hundred measures and transform the myriad kinds of things—this is what the "Canon of Shun" means by "align the seasons and the months and set the days correct, and unify the pitch pipes, measures, weights, and balances."
translations.idiomatic: That is why it can standardize every measure and give form to every thing—the very sense, in the "Canon of Shun," of "harmonizing the seasons, months, and intercalary days" and "making the pipes, lengths, pecks, and balances one system."

sentences.zh: 中聲節以成文，德音章而和備，則可以動天地，感鬼神，道性情，移風俗。

translations.literal: The mid-tone, cut to make patterned sound, displays virtuous timbre until harmony is complete; then it can move Heaven and Earth, stir ghosts and spirits, guide nature and disposition, and shift customs.
translations.idiomatic: When that central tone is shaped into patterned music and virtue rings through it in full harmony, it can stir Heaven and earth, move spirits, speak to human feeling, and remake the temper of a people.

sentences.zh: 葉言志於詠歌，鑒盛衰於治亂，故君子審聲以知音，審音以知樂，審樂以知政，蓋由茲道。

translations.literal: Thus intent is lodged in songs of praise, and the rise and fall of order and chaos can be mirrored in listening; therefore the gentleman examines sound to know tone, examines tone to know music, examines music to know policy—by this path.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry lodges the mind in song; order and chaos leave their echo in what we hear. That is why a cultivated man studies sound to grasp tone, tone to grasp music, and music to grasp how the realm is governed—always along this same path.

sentences.zh: 太史公律書云：「王者制事立物，法度軌則，一稟於六律。

translations.literal: The Grand Scribe's treatise on pitch says: "The king, in ordering affairs and establishing things, in laws, norms, tracks, and models, takes everything from the six pitch pipes."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's treatise on the pipes insists that the king, whenever he fixes rites or fashions tools—every statute, gauge, and model—grounds them all in the six yang pipes.

sentences.zh: 六律為萬事之本，其于兵械尤所重焉。

translations.literal: The six pipes are the root of the myriad tasks; for weapons and armor they are especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Those six pipes underlie every undertaking; they weigh heaviest of all on arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 故云望敵知吉凶，聞聲效勝負，百王不易之道也。」

translations.literal: Hence it is said: facing the enemy you know fortune or misfortune from them; hearing the army's note you can tell victory or defeat—this is a way no line of kings has changed."
translations.idiomatic: Men say you can read an army's luck by scanning the foe and judge victory or defeat by the note that rides the wind—a principle no dynasty has seen fit to abandon."

sentences.zh: 及秦氏滅學，其道浸微。

translations.literal: By the time the house of Qin annihilated learning, this teaching slowly faded.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin burned the books, that tradition nearly died away.

sentences.zh: 漢室初興，丞相張蒼首言律，未能審備。

translations.literal: When the Han first rose, Chancellor Zhang Cang was the first to speak on pitch pipes, yet he could not nail down every detail.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han, Chancellor Zhang Cang reopened the discussion of pitch, but his work still left gaps.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝創置協律之官，司馬遷言律呂相生之次詳矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu then created the office of pitch harmonizer, and Sima Qian set out the order in which the pipes beget one another with great thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han added a harmonics bureau, and Sima Qian traced, pipe by pipe, how each tone generates the next.

sentences.zh: 及王莽際，考論音律，劉歆條奏，大率有五：一曰備數，一、十、百、千、萬也；

translations.literal: At Wang Mang's time they reviewed musical theory; Liu Xin submitted a memorial listing five headings: first, "complete numbers"—one, ten, hundred, thousand, and ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang the court re-examined acoustics, and Liu Xin's memorial broke the system into five rubrics. The first was "numbering in full"—the powers from one through ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 二曰和聲，宮、商、角、徵、羽也；

translations.literal: second, "harmonized sounds"—gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu;
translations.idiomatic: the second was "matching the five notes"—gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu;

sentences.zh: 三曰審度，分、寸、尺、丈、引也；

translations.literal: third, "careful measurement"—fen, cun, chi, zhang, and yin;
translations.idiomatic: the third was "measured lengths"—from the fen up through the yin;

sentences.zh: 四曰嘉量，龠、合、升、鬥、斛也；

translations.literal: fourth, "commendable capacity"—yue, ge, sheng, dou, and hu;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth was "honest dry and wet measures"—from the yue up to the hu;

sentences.zh: 五曰權衡，銖、兩、斤、鈞、石也。

translations.literal: fifth, "weights and balances"—zhu, liang, jin, jun, and shi.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth was "weights and steelyards"—from the zhu to the shi stone.

sentences.zh: 班固因而志之。

translations.literal: Ban Gu therefore recorded them in his monograph.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu folded that scheme into his "Treatise on Pitch and Calendar."

sentences.zh: 蔡邕又記建武已後言律呂者，至司馬紹統采而續之。

translations.literal: Cai Yong next wrote up those who discussed pitch pipes after the Jianwu era, down to Sima Shaotong, who gathered the material and carried it forward.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong continued the story for the Eastern Han after Jianwu, and Sima Biao later collected and extended every note on the subject.

sentences.zh: 漢末天下大亂，樂工散亡，器法堙滅，魏武始獲杜夔，使定樂器聲調。

translations.literal: At the end of Han the realm dissolved in chaos; musicians scattered and perished, and the instruments and their methods were buried in oblivion. Cao Cao was the first to recover Du Kui and charge him with fixing the tuning of ritual instruments.
translations.idiomatic: When Han collapsed, players fled and died, carrying their craft to the grave. Only with Cao Cao did the court recover Du Kui and task him with resetting the orchestra.

sentences.zh: 夔依當時尺度，權備典章。

translations.literal: Du Kui relied on the scales then in use and provisionally restored the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui worked from contemporary foot-rules and patched the code back into service.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受命，遵而不革。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin received the mandate, he followed Du's system without reforming it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne, he kept Du Kui's tuning unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至泰始十年，光祿大夫荀勖奏造新度，更鑄律呂。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Taishi era, Minister of the Imperial Household Xun Xi memorialized for new measures and a fresh casting of the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 10 the household minister Xun Xi asked to cast new bronze pipes from a revised measure.

sentences.zh: 元康中，勖子籓嗣其事，未及成功，屬永嘉之亂，中朝典章，咸沒于石勒。

translations.literal: During the Yuankang years Xun's son Xun Fan inherited the project; before it could succeed the Yongjia disaster struck, and the archives of the central court all fell into Shi Le's hands.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang his son Xun Fan took over, but Yongjia's sack of Luoyang swallowed the capital's libraries before the work was finished, and Shi Le seized what survived.

sentences.zh: 及元帝南遷，皇度草昧，禮容樂器，掃地皆盡，雖稍加采掇，而多所淪胥，終於恭、安，竟不能備。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan moved south, imperial norms were still raw; ritual vestments and instruments were swept away. Although something was later gathered up, much had sunk beyond recovery, and down through Emperors Gong and An the set was never made whole again.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan fled south the court barely had a wardrobe or band left. Later reigns scraped together odds and ends, yet most pieces never surfaced again, and by the reigns of Gong and An the old orchestra could not be restored.

sentences.zh: 今考古律相生之次，及魏武已後言音律度量者，以聲明於篇雲。

translations.literal: Here I examine the sequence in which the ancient pipes beget one another, together with everyone from Cao Cao onward who spoke on pitch, tone, and measure, and set the matter forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: What follows collates the classical cycle of generating pipes with every major Jin-era discussion of acoustics and metrology from Cao Cao on.

sentences.zh: 《傳》云：「十二律，黃帝之所作也。

translations.literal: The traditions say: "The twelve pitch pipes were devised by the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The lore runs: "The Yellow Emperor fashioned the twelve pipes."

sentences.zh: 使伶倫自大夏之西，乃之昆侖之陰，取竹之嶰穀生，其竅厚均者，斷雨節間長三寸九分而吹之，以為黃鐘之宮，曰含少。

translations.literal: He sent Ling Lun west of Great Xia, to the shaded north of Kunlun, took bamboo from the Xie Valley whose bore and walls were even, cut two nodes to leave a segment three cun nine fen long, blew it, and took it as the Yellow Bell's palace tone, naming it Hánshǎo.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ling Lun beyond Great Xia to Kunlun's north slope, chose even-gauge bamboo from the Xie Valley gorge, cut a tube three cun nine fen between nodes, sounded it, and fixed the Yellow Bell's fundamental under the name Hánshǎo.

sentences.zh: 次制十二竹筒，寫鳳之鳴，雄鳴為六，雌鳴亦六，以比黃鐘之宮，皆可以生之以定律呂。

translations.literal: Next he fashioned twelve bamboo tubes, copying the phoenix's cry—six calls from the male, six from the female—and matched them to the Yellow Bell's fundamental so that every pipe could generate the others and complete the scale.
translations.idiomatic: He then bored twelve bamboo pipes, imitating the cock and hen phoenix—six tones each—and keyed them to the Yellow Bell so the whole chromatic set could be spun off from that root.

sentences.zh: 則律之始造，以竹為管，取其自然圓虛也。

translations.literal: Thus at the first creation of the pipes bamboo was used for the tube, taking advantage of its natural roundness and hollowness.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the earliest pipes were bamboo: the material is already a perfect hollow cylinder.

sentences.zh: 」又云「黃帝作律，以玉為管，長尺，六孔，這二十月音。

translations.literal: " It is also said: "The Yellow Emperor made pitch pipes from jade, one chi long, with six holes, matching the tones of the twelve months (the received text is corrupt at this point)."
translations.idiomatic: Another line adds that the Yellow Emperor cut jade pipes a foot long with six holes—one for each month of the year—though the wording in our manuscript is damaged here.

sentences.zh: 至舜時，西王母獻昭華之琯，以玉為之。

translations.literal: By Shun's time the Queen Mother of the West presented the Zhāohuá pipes, likewise made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: At Shun's court the Queen Mother of the West sent the "Radiant Splendor" jade flutes.

sentences.zh: 」及漢章帝時，零陵文學奚景於泠道舜祠下得白玉琯。

translations.literal: " In the time of Han Emperor Zhang, the Lingling scholar Xi Jing found a white jade pipe in the Shun shrine at Lengdao.
translations.idiomatic: During Han Zhangdi's reign the classicist Xi Jing of Lingling pulled a white jade pitch pipe from Shun's temple at Lengdao.

sentences.zh: 又武帝太康元年，汲郡盜發六國時魏襄王塚，亦得玉律。

translations.literal: Again, in the first year of Emperor Wu's Taikang era, tomb robbers opened the grave of King Xiang of Wei from the Warring States period in Ji commandery and also recovered jade pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Wudi's Taikang 1 plunderers who broke into King Xiang of Wei's Warring States tomb at Ji commandery likewise turned up jade tuning pipes.

sentences.zh: 則古者又以玉為管矣。

translations.literal: Thus in antiquity jade was also used for the tubes.
translations.idiomatic: So the ancients sometimes tuned in jade as well as bamboo.

sentences.zh: 以玉者，取其體含廉潤也。

translations.literal: With jade they sought a substance that holds moist luster within.
translations.idiomatic: Jade was prized because its body seems to drink in a cool, even gleam.

sentences.zh: 而漢平帝時，王莽又以銅為之。

translations.literal: Yet under Han Emperor Ping, Wang Mang again had them cast in bronze.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han's child emperor Ping, Wang Mang ordered a bronze set.

sentences.zh: 銅者，自名也，所以同天下，齊風俗也。

translations.literal: Bronze speaks for itself: it was how the realm could share one standard and align every custom.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze advertised a single public standard—metal the whole country could copy so customs would line up.

sentences.zh: 為物至精，不為燥濕寒暑改節，介然有常，似士君子之行，故用焉。

translations.literal: As a material it is supremely refined; it does not shift its pitch with dryness, wetness, cold, or heat, but stands firm and constant, like the conduct of a gentleman—therefore it was employed.
translations.idiomatic: It is a stuff so stable that heat, damp, and frost barely pull its note—steady as a gentleman's bearing—which is why later courts preferred it.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》太師掌六律、六呂，以合陰陽之聲。

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou" says the Grand Master of Music holds the six yang pipes and six yin pipes to join the sounds of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" puts the Grand Master of Music in charge of six yang and six yin pipes so the bright and dark registers answer each other.

sentences.zh: 六律陽聲，黃鐘、太蔟、姑洗、蕤賓、夷則、無射也；

translations.literal: The six yang tones are Yellow Bell, Great Budding, Guǌxǐ, Ruíbīn, Yízé, and Wúyì;
translations.idiomatic: The six yang pipes are Yellow Bell, Tàicù, Gǔxǐ, Ruíbīn, Yízé, and Wúyì;

sentences.zh: 六呂陰聲，大呂、應鐘、南呂、林鐘、仲呂、夾鐘也。

translations.literal: the six yin tones are Great Regulator, Bell of Response, Southern Regulator, Forest Bell, Zhònglǚ, and Jiázhōng.
translations.idiomatic: the six yin pipes are Dàlǚ, Yìngzhōng, Nánlǚ, Línzhōng, Zhònglǚ, and Jiázhōng.

sentences.zh: 又有太師則執同律以聽軍聲，而詔以吉凶。

translations.literal: Again, when the Grand Master of Music campaigns he grasps the pitch pipe to listen to the army's note and thereby proclaims good or ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign the same officer carries a uniform pipe to listen to the troops' hum and read Heaven's verdict.

sentences.zh: 其典同掌六律之和，以辯天地四方陰陽之聲，以為樂器，皆以十有二律而為之數度，以十有二聲而為之齊量焉。

translations.literal: The office of Diǎntóng harmonizes the six pipes, discriminates the sounds of Heaven, earth, and the four quarters into yin and yang registers, and fashions musical instruments: every measure derives from the twelve pipes, every balance from the twelve timbres.
translations.idiomatic: The Diǎntóng office blends the six pipes, sorts the tones of heaven, earth, and the four directions into yin and yang, and builds instruments whose lengths and volumes all count out in twelves.

sentences.zh: 及周景王將鑄無射，問律於泠州鳩，對曰：「夫六，中之色，故名之曰黃鐘，所以宣養六氣九德也。

translations.literal: When King Jing of Zhou was about to cast the Wúyì bell, he asked about pitch from Leng Zhoujiu, who replied: "As for six: it is the color of the center; therefore it is called Yellow Bell, whereby the six qi and the nine virtues are announced and nourished.
translations.idiomatic: Planning the Wúyì bell for Zhou, King Jing questioned Lěng Zhōujiū, who answered: "Yellow stands for the central element—hence the fundamental pipe is named Yellow Bell, the voice that broadcasts and feeds the six vapors and nine virtues."

sentences.zh: 由是第之。

translations.literal: From this he ranked them.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he ordered the scale.

sentences.zh: 二曰太蔟，所以金奏贊陽出滯也。

translations.literal: Second is Tàicù, whereby metal performances praise the yang and draw the pent-up forth.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes Tàicù, the pipe that drives bronze fanfares, lifts the yang qi, and shakes off stagnation.

sentences.zh: 三曰姑洗，所以羞潔百物，考神納賓也。

translations.literal: Third is Gǔxǐ, whereby things are purified in offering, spirits examined, and guests welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: Third is Gǔxǐ, used to rinse offerings clean, draw spirits down, and welcome guests.

sentences.zh: 四曰蕤賓，所以安靜神人，獻酬交酢也。

translations.literal: Fourth is Ruíbīn, whereby spirits and men are calmed and toasts are exchanged in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth is Ruíbīn, the pitch of quiet worship and of pledging cup after cup.

sentences.zh: 五曰夷則，所以詠歌九德，平人無貳也。

translations.literal: Fifth is Yízé, whereby the nine virtues are sung in hymns and the people are kept from duplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth is Yízé, the tone on which the nine virtues are hymned and common folk kept single-hearted.

sentences.zh: 六曰無射，所以宣佈哲人之令德，示人軌儀也。

translations.literal: Sixth is Wúyì, whereby the bright commands of the wise are proclaimed and models for conduct displayed to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth is Wúyì, the pipe that proclaims a sage-king's shining edicts and shows the people their compass.

sentences.zh: 為之六間，以揚沈伏而黜散越也。

translations.literal: Between them lie six interstices to float what sinks too deep and prune what scatters too wide.
translations.idiomatic: Six intercalary pipes sit between them to lift what lies too deep and trim what flies too loose.

sentences.zh: 元間大呂，助宣物也，二間夾鐘，出四隙之細也。

translations.literal: The first interstice is Dàlǚ, which helps propagate the myriad things; the second is Jiázhōng, which lets the fine detail slip through the four gaps.
translations.idiomatic: The first gap is Dàlǚ, pushing the year's growth outward; the second is Jiázhōng, threading the subtlest filigree through the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 三間中呂，宣中氣也。

translations.literal: The third is Zhònglǚ, which vents the central qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhònglǚ is the third slot, venting the qi that pools at the year's hinge.

sentences.zh: 四間林鐘，和展百事，俾莫不任肅純恪也。

translations.literal: The fourth is Línzhōng, which harmonizes the hundred affairs so that none fail to rise in solemn purity.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth is Línzhōng, harmonizing every task of state so each is met with reverent care.

sentences.zh: 五間南呂，贊陽秀也。

translations.literal: The fifth is Nánlǚ, which assists the flowering of the yang.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth is Nánlǚ, coaxing the yang into full bloom.

sentences.zh: 六間應鐘，均利器用，俾應復也。

translations.literal: The sixth is Yìngzhōng, which evens sharp tools and responses so that the cycle can begin again.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth is Yìngzhōng, evening implements and echoes so the circuit can close and reopen."

sentences.zh: 」此皆所以律述時氣效節物也。

translations.literal: " All this is how the pipes track seasonal qi and mirror the things of each month.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of those pipes is a calendar in sound, pegging the month's qi to a note.

sentences.zh: 及秦始皇焚書蕩覆，典策缺亡，諸子瑣言時有遺記。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor of Qin burned the books and overturned the tradition, canons and records were lost, though stray sentences of the masters occasionally survived.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang's bonfire scattered the classics; only stray glosses survived in the philosophers.

sentences.zh: 呂不韋《春秋》言：黃鐘之宮，律之本也，下生林鐘，林鐘上生太蔟，太蔟下生南呂，南呂上生姑洗，姑洗下生應鐘，應鐘上生蕤賓，蕤賓下生大呂，大呂下生夷則，夷則上生夾鐘，夾鐘下生無射，無射上生中呂。

translations.literal: Lü Buwei's "Spring and Autumn of Lü" states: The Yellow Bell's palace is the root of the pipes; downward it begets Forest Bell; Forest Bell upward begets Tàicù; Tàicù downward begets Southern Regulator; Southern Regulator upward begets Gǔxǐ; Gǔxǐ downward begets Bell of Response; Bell of Response upward begets Ruíbīn; Ruíbīn downward begets Great Regulator; Great Regulator downward begets Yízé; Yízé upward begets Jiázhōng; Jiázhōng downward begets Wúyì; Wúyì upward begets Zhònglǚ.
translations.idiomatic: The "Lüshi chunqiu" still preserves the full circle: Yellow Bell down to Forest Bell, Forest Bell up to Tàicù, and so on through the twelve—each third generates the next by adding or subtracting a third of its length.

sentences.zh: 三分所生，益其一分以上生；

translations.literal: Of the thirds produced, increase one third to ascend a generation;
translations.idiomatic: When a pipe "ascends," you lengthen the tube by one third of its predecessor;

sentences.zh: 三分所生，去其一分以下生。

translations.literal: of the thirds produced, remove one third to descend a generation.
translations.idiomatic: when it "descends," you shorten it by one third.

sentences.zh: 後代之言音律者多宗此說。

translations.literal: Later writers on acoustics mostly follow this doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later acousticians nearly all hew to that rule of thirds.

sentences.zh: 及漢興，承秦之弊，張蒼首治律曆，頗未能詳。

translations.literal: When Han arose it inherited Qin's ruin; Zhang Cang was first to work on pitch and calendar, yet still left much unclear.
translations.idiomatic: The Han began in Qin's rubble: Zhang Cang reopened pitch and calendrics but left the fine points fuzzy.

sentences.zh: 故孝武帝正樂，乃置協律之官，雖律呂清濁之體粗正，金石高下之音有准，然徒捃采遺存，以成一時之制，而數猶用五。

translations.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu set music aright he created the harmonizer's office; although the body of clear and muddy pitch was roughly corrected and the highs and lows of metal and stone gained a standard, they merely gathered what scraps survived to patch a system for the moment, and the arithmetic still relied on five.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu "rectified" music he added harmonizers—enough to sort bronze and stone into something like tune—but the court was really collating debris, and the math still ran on fives.

sentences.zh: 時淮南王安延致儒博，亦為律呂。

translations.literal: At that time Liu An, the king of Huainan, gathered broad scholars and likewise composed a treatise on the pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu An of Huainan patronized scholars and wrote his own pipe treatise.

sentences.zh: 雲黃鐘之律九寸而宮音調，因而九之，九九八十一，故黃鐘之數立焉，位在子。

translations.literal: It says: The Yellow Bell pipe measures nine cun and tunes the gong note; multiplying by nine yields eighty-one, so the Yellow Bell's number is fixed, stationed at the branch zi.
translations.idiomatic: There the Yellow Bell tube is nine cun long and anchors gong; nine times nine gives eighty-one, fixing its numerology on the branch zi.

sentences.zh: 林鐘位在未，其數五十四。

translations.literal: Forest Bell sits at wèi with the number fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell sits on wèi with fifty-four as its tally.

sentences.zh: 太蔟其數七十二，南呂之數四十八，姑洗之數六十四，應鐘之數四十二，蕤賓之數五十七，大呂之數七十六，夷則之數五十一，夾鐘之數六十八，無射之數四十五，中呂之數六十，極不生。

translations.literal: Tàicù has seventy-two, Southern Regulator forty-eight, Gǔxǐ sixty-four, Bell of Response forty-two, Ruíbīn fifty-seven, Great Regulator seventy-six, Yízé fifty-one, Jiázhōng sixty-eight, Wúyì forty-five, Zhònglǚ sixty—and at the limit nothing further is born.
translations.idiomatic: The chain runs Tàicù seventy-two, Southern Regulator forty-eight, Gǔxǐ sixty-four, Yìngzhōng forty-two, Ruíbīn fifty-seven, Dàlǚ seventy-six, Yízé fifty-one, Jiázhōng sixty-eight, Wúyì forty-five, Zhònglǚ sixty, ending where the cycle cannot generate another pipe.

sentences.zh: 以黃鐘為宮，太蔟為商，姑洗為角，林鐘為徽，南呂為羽。

translations.literal: Taking Yellow Bell as gong, Tàicù as shang, Gǔxǐ as jue, Forest Bell as zhi, and Southern Regulator as yu.
translations.idiomatic: Those pipes map to the pentatonic set: gong on Yellow Bell, shang on Tàicù, jue on Gǔxǐ, zhi on Forest Bell, yu on Southern Regulator.

sentences.zh: 宮生徵，徵生商，商生羽，羽生角，角生應鐘，不比正音，故為和；

translations.literal: Gong begets zhi, zhi begets shang, shang begets yu, yu begets jue; jue begets Bell of Response, which is not a principal degree, hence is called the "harmony";
translations.idiomatic: From gong you derive zhi, then shang, yu, and jue; jue slips down to Yìngzhōng, outside the core pentatonic, so the Huainan writers dub that link "harmony";

sentences.zh: 應鐘生蕤賓，不比正音，故為繆。

translations.literal: Bell of Response begets Ruíbīn, likewise not a principal degree, hence is called the "wavering".
translations.idiomatic: Yìngzhōng in turn feeds Ruíbīn—again off the main five—so they call that second step "wavering."

sentences.zh: 日冬至，音比林鐘浸以濁。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice the note tends toward Forest Bell and grows muddy.
translations.idiomatic: On the longest night the pitch slides toward Forest Bell and thickens toward mud.

sentences.zh: 日夏至，音比黃鐘浸以清。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice the note tends toward Yellow Bell and grows clear.
translations.idiomatic: On the shortest night it slides toward Yellow Bell and thins toward ice.

sentences.zh: 十二律應二十四時之變。

translations.literal: The twelve pipes answer the twenty-four seasonal nodes.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pipes answer the twenty-four qi nodes of the year.

sentences.zh: 甲子，中呂之徵也。

translations.literal: The jiǎzǐ day is the zhi tone of Zhònglǚ.
translations.idiomatic: A jiǎzǐ day rides Zhònglǚ's zhi voice.

sentences.zh: 丙子，夾鐘之羽也。

translations.literal: The bǐngzǐ day is the yu tone of Jiázhōng.
translations.idiomatic: A bǐngzǐ day rides Jiázhōng's yu voice.

sentences.zh: 戊子，黃鐘之宮也。

translations.literal: The wùzǐ day is the gong of Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: A wùzǐ day sits on Yellow Bell's gong.

sentences.zh: 庚子，無射之商也。

translations.literal: The gēngzǐ day is the shang of Wúyì.
translations.idiomatic: A gēngzǐ day carries Wúyì's shang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，夷則之角也。

translations.literal: The rénzǐ day is the jue of Yízé.
translations.idiomatic: A rénzǐ day takes Yízé's jue.

sentences.zh: 其為音也，一律而生五音，十二律而為六十音。

translations.literal: As for their sounds, one pipe yields the five degrees, and twelve pipes yield sixty notes.
translations.idiomatic: Each fundamental spawns the five degrees; twelve fundamentals spin sixty changing notes.

sentences.zh: 因而六之，六六三十六，故三百六十音以當一歲之日。

translations.literal: Multiplying again by six, six times six is thirty-six, so three hundred sixty notes match the days of a year.
translations.idiomatic: Sixfold iteration—six times six thirty-six—maps three hundred sixty mutations onto the three hundred sixty days.

sentences.zh: 故律曆之數，天地之道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the numbers of pitch and calendar are the Way of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: That is why acoustics and the calendar share one mathematics—the weave of Heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 司馬遷八書言律呂，粗舉大經，著于前史。

translations.literal: In his eight treatises Sima Qian discusses pitch pipes, sketching only the great outline, as earlier histories record.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's eight monographs already roughed out the theory, as the earlier standard histories show.

sentences.zh: 則以太極元氣函三為一，而始動於子，十二律之生，必所起焉。

translations.literal: There the Grand Ultimate's primal qi enfolds three in one; it first stirs at zi, and the birth of the twelve pipes must begin from there.
translations.idiomatic: There the primordial taiji breath wraps triads in unity; motion begins at the branch zi, and the twelve pipes must germinate from that gate.

sentences.zh: 於是參一於醜得三，因而九三之，舉本位合十辰，得一萬九千六百八十三，謂之成數，以為黃鐘之法。

translations.literal: Thereupon tripling one against chǒu yields three; multiplying by nine thrice and raising the base to combine with the ten stems produces 19,683, called the "completion number," taken as Yellow Bell's divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Tripling one against chǒu, then compounding nines across the stem cycle, lands on 19,683—the "full divisor" canonized for Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 又參之律於十二辰，得十七萬七千一百四十七，謂之該數，以為黃鐘之實。

translations.literal: Tripling again against the twelve branches yields 177,147, called the "encompassing number," taken as Yellow Bell's dividend.
translations.idiomatic: Run the same ladder against all twelve branches and you reach 177,147, the "total dividend" stored inside Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 實如法而一，得黃鐘之律長九寸，十一月冬至之氣應焉。

translations.literal: Dividing dividend by divisor yields one; hence the Yellow Bell pipe is nine cun long, answering the qi of the winter solstice in the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the inner total by the outer and the sounding length comes out nine cun—the pipe that answers the eleventh month's winter solstice breath.

sentences.zh: 蓋陰陽合德，氣鐘於子，而化生萬物，則物之生莫不函三。

translations.literal: Where yin and yang share virtue, qi gathers at zi and transforms the myriad things, and nothing born but enfolds a triad.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang meet their virtue in zi, where qi knits the myriad things, each triply seeded.

sentences.zh: 故十二律空徑三分，而上下相生，皆損益以三。

translations.literal: Therefore the twelve pipes have a bore of three fen, and upper and lower generations all gain or lose by thirds.
translations.idiomatic: Hence every classical pipe keeps a three-fen bore, and each generation up or down the cycle lengthens or shortens by a third.

sentences.zh: 其術則因黃鐘之長九寸，以下生者倍其實，三其法：以上生者，四其實，三其法。

translations.literal: The method is: starting from Yellow Bell's length of nine cun, for a descending generation double the dividend and triple the divisor; for an ascending generation quadruple the dividend and triple the divisor.
translations.idiomatic: The algorithm says: from the nine-cun Yellow Bell, descend by doubling the numerator while tripling the denominator, or ascend by quadrupling while still tripling the denominator—

sentences.zh: 所以明陽下生陰，陰上生陽。

translations.literal: thereby clarifying how yang descends to beget yin and yin ascends to beget yang.
translations.idiomatic: which is how yang notes beget yin and yin notes climb back to beget yang.

sentences.zh: 起子，為黃鐘九寸，一。

translations.literal: Beginning from the branch zi, Yellow Bell is nine cun long—value one.
translations.idiomatic: At zi the Yellow Bell line starts: a tube nine cun long, taken as unity.

sentences.zh: 醜，三分之二。

translations.literal: Chou: two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: For chǒu the ratio is two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 寅，九分之八。

translations.literal: Yin: eight-ninths.
translations.idiomatic: For yín the ratio is eight-ninths.

sentences.zh: 卯，二十七分之十六。

translations.literal: Mao: sixteen twenty-sevenths.
translations.idiomatic: For mǎo it is sixteen parts out of twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 辰，八十一分之六十四。

translations.literal: Chen: sixty-four eighty-firsts.
translations.idiomatic: For chén, sixty-four over eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 巳，二百四十三分之一百二十八。

translations.literal: Si: one hundred twenty-eight two hundred forty-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: For sì, one hundred twenty-eight parts in two hundred forty-three.

sentences.zh: 午，七百二十九分之五百一十二。

translations.literal: Wu: five hundred twelve seven hundred twenty-ninths.
translations.idiomatic: For wǔ, five hundred twelve over seven hundred twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 未，二千一百八十七分之一千二十四。

translations.literal: Wei: one thousand twenty-four two thousand one hundred eighty-sevenths.
translations.idiomatic: For wèi, one thousand twenty-four over two thousand one hundred eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 申，六千五百六十一分之四千九十六。

translations.literal: Shen: four thousand ninety-six six thousand five hundred sixty-firsts.
translations.idiomatic: For shēn, four thousand ninety-six over six thousand five hundred sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 酉，一萬九千六百八十二分之八千一百九十二。

translations.literal: You: eight thousand one hundred ninety-two nineteen thousand six hundred eighty-second parts.
translations.idiomatic: For yǒu, eight thousand one hundred ninety-two parts in nineteen thousand six hundred eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 戌，五萬九千四十九分之三萬二千七百六十八。

translations.literal: Xu: thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight fifty-nine thousand forty-ninth parts.
translations.idiomatic: For xū, thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight over fifty-nine thousand forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 亥，十七萬七千一百四十七分之六萬五千五百三十六。

translations.literal: Hai: sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seventh parts.
translations.idiomatic: For hài, sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six over one hundred seventy-seven thousand one hundred forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 如是周十二辰，在六律為陽，則當位自得而下生陰，在六呂為陰，則得其所衡而上生於陽，推算之術無重上生之法也。

translations.literal: Thus, completing the twelve branches: among the six yang pipes each occupies its proper station and naturally downward begets yin; among the six yin pipes each obtains its matched counterpart and upward begets yang; in the reckoning of derivation there is no method of 'ascending again.'
translations.idiomatic: Run the circuit of twelve branches and you see the rule: each yang pipe sits in its own seat and drops a third to sire yin; each yin pipe reaches across to its partner and climbs a third to sire yang—and nowhere does the math allow a second consecutive ascent.

sentences.zh: 所謂律取妻，呂生子，陰陽升降，律呂之大經也。

translations.literal: This is what is called 'the pitch pipe takes a wife, the note bears a son'—yin and yang rising and falling: the great constant of pipes and notes.
translations.idiomatic: That is the old formula 'yang pipes wed, yin notes bear children'—the rise and fall of yin and yang that governs every pipe relationship.

sentences.zh: 而遷又言十二律之長，今依淮南九九之數，則蕤賓為重上。

translations.literal: Yet Sima Qian also says that for the lengths of the twelve pipes, if one now follows the Huainan 'nine-nines' reckoning, then Ruíbīn suffers a double ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian adds that, measured by the Huainan nine-times table, Ruíbīn would be asked to 'ascend twice,' which breaks the rule.

sentences.zh: 又言五音相生，而以宮生角，角生商，商生徵，徵生羽，羽生宮。

translations.literal: He also describes the five notes' mutual generation as gong begetting jue, jue begetting shang, shang begetting zhi, zhi begetting yu, yu begetting gong.
translations.idiomatic: He also orders the pentatonic cycle as gong → jue → shang → zhi → yu → gong—a sequence that does not match the thirds method.

sentences.zh: 求其理用，罔見通途。

translations.literal: Seeking its rationale in use, one never sees a clear through-road.
translations.idiomatic: Applied to practice, that account never lines up end to end.

sentences.zh: 及元始中，王莽輔政，博征通知鐘律者，考其音義，使羲和劉歆典領調奏。

translations.literal: In the Yuanshi era Wang Mang directed the government; broadly summoning men who understood bells and pitch pipes, he examined their sounds and meanings and had the Xihe official Liu Xin take charge of tuning and memorial submission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang's Yuanshi regency the court cast a wide net for acousticians, reviewed their theories, and put Liu Xin of the Xihe office in charge of the tuning project.

sentences.zh: 班固《漢書》采而志之，其序論雖博，而言十二律損益次第，自黃鐘長九寸，三分損一，下生林鐘，長六寸。

translations.literal: Ban Gu's 'Book of Han' adopted and recorded this; although his preface is wide-ranging, when he lists the order of subtracting and adding thirds among the twelve pipes—from Yellow Bell at nine cun long, 'subtracting one third' downward to beget Forest Bell at six cun—
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu folded Liu Xin's work into the Hanshu monograph: his introduction is learned, yet the step-by-step thirds—Yellow Bell at nine cun, subtract a third down to Forest Bell at six cun—

sentences.zh: 三分益一，上生太蔟而左旋，八八為位。

translations.literal: 'adding one third' upward begets Tàicù, turning leftward, with eight times eight fixing the positions.
translations.idiomatic: then add a third up to Tàicù, wheel counterclockwise, and let eight-times-eight mark each station—

sentences.zh: 一上一下，終於無射，下生中呂。

translations.literal: one ascent, one descent, ending at Wúyì, then downward begets Zhònglǚ.
translations.idiomatic: each step alternating up and down until Wúyì, then the last descent lands on Zhònglǚ.

sentences.zh: 校其相生所得，與司馬遷正同。

translations.literal: Checking the mutual-generation totals shows they match Sima Qian exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Carry the arithmetic through and you land on the same lengths Sima Qian gave.

sentences.zh: 班固采以為志。

translations.literal: Ban Gu adopted this for his treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu took that scheme as his standard.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，郎中京房知五音六十律之數，上使太子傅玄成、諫議大夫章雜試問房于樂府，房對：「受學于故小黃令焦延壽。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan, court gentleman Jing Fang knew the mathematics of the five notes and sixty pipes; the emperor sent the heir's tutor Xuan Cheng and grand counsellor of remonstrance Zhang Za to examine Fang at the music office. Fang replied: 'I studied under the former prefect of Lesser Huang, Jiao Yanshou.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan had Jing Fang—who had mastered the sixty-pipe extension of the pentatonic set—interrogated at the imperial music bureau by Xuan Cheng and Zhang Za; Fang said he had learned the art from Jiao Yanshou, the former Lesser Huang prefect.

sentences.zh: 六十律相生之法：以上生下，皆三生二；

translations.literal: The sixty-pipes mutual-generation method: to engender lower from upper, in every case three engenders two;
translations.idiomatic: Fang's rule for stepping down: from a longer parent pipe, three always begets two;

sentences.zh: 以下生上，皆三生四。

translations.literal: to engender upper from lower, in every case three engenders four.
translations.idiomatic: for stepping up, three always begets four.

sentences.zh: 陽下生陰，陰上生陽，終於中呂，而十二律畢矣。

translations.literal: Yang downward begets yin, yin upward begets yang; ending at Zhònglǚ, the twelve pipes are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yang drops to yin, yin climbs back to yang, and the ring closes on Zhònglǚ with the classical twelve.

sentences.zh: 中呂上生執始，執始下生去滅。

translations.literal: Zhònglǚ upward begets Zhǐshǐ, Zhǐshǐ downward begets Qùmiè.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhònglǚ the cycle continues up to Zhǐshǐ and down to Qùmiè—

sentences.zh: 上下相生，終於南事，而六十律畢矣。

translations.literal: upper and lower generation end at Nánshì, and the sixty pipes are complete.
translations.idiomatic: —until Nánshì finishes the fifth layer of splits and the full sixty names are filled out.

sentences.zh: 夫十二律之變至於六十，猶八卦之變至於六十四也。

translations.literal: As the twelve pipes ramify to sixty, so the eight trigrams ramify to sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pipes unfolding to sixty parallels the eight trigrams unfolding to sixty-four lines.

sentences.zh: 宓犧作《易》，紀陽氣之初以為律法。

translations.literal: Fuxi composed the 'Changes,' recording the first breath of yang qi to establish the model for pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi wrote the "Zhouyi" by pinning the first yang breath of the year—the same logic that underlies the pipe numbers.

sentences.zh: 建日冬至之聲，以黃鐘為宮，太蔟為商，姑洗為角，林鐘為徽，南呂為羽，應鐘為變宮，蕤賓為變徵，此聲氣之元，五音之正也。

translations.literal: He set the sound for the winter-solstice day: Yellow Bell as gong, Tàicù as shang, Gǔxǐ as jue, Forest Bell as zhi, Southern Regulator as yu, Yìngzhōng as altered gong, Ruíbīn as altered zhi—these are the root of musical qi and the true pentatonic degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He keyed the winter solstice to Yellow Bell on gong, Tàicù on shang, Gǔxǐ on jue, Forest Bell on zhi, Southern Regulator on yu, with Yìngzhōng and Ruíbīn as the two altered steps—the seed tones of the whole system.

sentences.zh: 故各統一日，其餘以次運行，當日者各自為宮，而商角徽羽以類從焉。

translations.literal: Therefore each name rules one day; the others rotate in sequence, and whichever day is 'in charge' becomes gong for itself, while shang, jue, zhi, and yu follow by category.
translations.idiomatic: Each pitch governs its own day while the others march around it; whichever pitch heads the day acts as temporary gong, and the four companions fall in by class.

sentences.zh: 《禮運》曰「五聲、六律、十二管還相為宮」，此之謂也。

translations.literal: The 'Record of Rites' says, 'The five timbres, six pitch sets, and twelve tubes take turns as gong'—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: That is the sense of the "Record of Rites" line that the five voices and twelve tubes 'revolve as gong.'

sentences.zh: 以六十律分期之日，黃鐘自冬至始，及冬至而復，陰陽、寒燠、風雨之占生焉。

translations.literal: Using the sixty pipes to divide the days of the period, Yellow Bell starts from the winter solstice and, when winter solstice returns, auguries of yin and yang, cold and warm, wind and rain arise from it.
translations.idiomatic: Mapping the sixty mutations across the year begins at the winter solstice node on Yellow Bell; when the node comes round again, you read yin-yang, temperature, and weather from the same cycle.

sentences.zh: 於以檢攝群音，考其高下，苟非革木之聲，則無不有所合。

translations.literal: Thereby one reins in the mass of notes, examining their highs and lows: unless it is the sound of leather or wood, nothing fails to find correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: With that grid you can police every instrument: aside from hide and wood drums, every timbre should click into one of the slots.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》曰「律和聲，此之謂也。」

translations.literal: The 'Canon of Shun' says, 'The pitch pipes harmonize the sounds'—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's canon meant exactly this when it said the pipes "harmonize the sounds."

sentences.zh: 京房又曰：「竹聲不可以度調，故作準以定數。

translations.literal: Jing Fang also said: 'The sound of bamboo cannot be regulated by measure, so I made a pitch-finder (zhun) to fix the numbers.'
translations.idiomatic: Fang added that bamboo notes cannot be cut by abstract measure alone, so he built a string "standard" (zhun) to nail the fractions down.

sentences.zh: 准之狀如瑟，而長丈，十三弦，隱間九尺，以應黃鐘之律九寸。

translations.literal: The zhun is shaped like a se zither but one zhang long, with thirteen strings; the hidden span is nine chi, matching the Yellow Bell pipe of nine cun.
translations.idiomatic: The device looks like a small se, a full zhàng in length, strung thirteen times across a sounding length of nine chǐ—mirroring the nine-cun Yellow Bell tube.

sentences.zh: 中央一弦，下有畫分寸，以為六十律清濁之節。

translations.literal: The center string bears painted fen and cun marks below it, to serve as nodes for clear and muddy across the sixty pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The middle string is ruled in fen and cun so every semitone in the sixtyfold cycle has a visible notch.

sentences.zh: 」房言律詳於歆所奏，其術施行于史官，候部用之，文多不悉載。

translations.literal: ' Fang's discussion of pitch is fuller than what Liu Xin submitted; his method was practiced by the clerks, used by the forecasting bureaus, and the text is too long to record fully here.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's treatise outruns Liu Xin's memorial; the observatories adopted his zhun even though the full proof is too long for this chapter.

sentences.zh: 截管為律，吹以考聲，列以效氣，道之本也。

translations.literal: Cutting a tube to make a pitch pipe, blowing to examine the note, arraying it to test the qi—this is the root of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Sawing a pipe, blowing to hear it, lining it up to read the qi—that is still the bedrock method.

sentences.zh: 術家以其聲微而體難知，其分數不明，故作準以代之。

translations.literal: Technicians, because the sound is faint and the body hard to know and the fractions unclear, therefore made the zhun as a substitute.
translations.idiomatic: Because a tube whispers and its bore is hard to measure, technicians reach for the string standard instead.

sentences.zh: 准之聲明暢易達，分寸又粗，然弦以緩急清濁，非管無以正也。

translations.literal: The zhun's tone is bright and easy to reach, and its fen and cun are comparatively coarse, yet strings by tightness or slackness set clear and muddy, and without a tube there is nothing to correct by.
translations.idiomatic: Strings speak clearly and coarse marks are easy to read, yet only a finished pipe can correct what the ear accepts as true pitch.

sentences.zh: 均其中弦，令與黃鐘相得，案畫以求諸律，則無不如數而應者矣。

translations.literal: Equal the center string so it answers Yellow Bell; then by the markings seek the other pitches, and none will fail to match the reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Match the middle string to Yellow Bell, trace the inked ticks outward, and every derived length falls on the predicted number.

sentences.zh: 《續漢志》具載其六十律准度數，其相生之次與《呂覽》、《淮南》同。

translations.literal: The 'Treatise on Later Han' fully records his sixty-pipe zhun measures; the order of mutual generation matches the 'Lü's Annals' and 'Huainanzi.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye's continuation of the Han treatise preserves every zhun length; the breeding order matches both the "Lüshi chunqiu" and the "Huainanzi."

sentences.zh: 漢章帝元和元年，待詔候鐘律殷肜上言：「官無曉六十律以准調音者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Zhang's Yuanhe era, expectant official Yin Rong, who supervised bells and pipes, submitted: 'The office has no one who can use the sixty pipes with the zhun to tune notes.'
translations.idiomatic: In Han Zhangdi's Yuanhe 1 the expectant official Yin Rong, charged with bells and pipes, reported that no musician left could align the sixty mutations with Fang's string standard.

sentences.zh: 故待詔嚴崇具以准法教子男宣，原召宣補學官，主調樂器。

translations.literal: Therefore expectant official Yan Chong fully taught the zhun method to his son Xuan; I ask that Xuan be summoned to fill a study post and take charge of tuning instruments.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chong had already drilled the method into his son Xuan; Yin asked the throne to call Xuan in as a student officer to tune the orchestra.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「崇子學審曉律，別其族，協其聲者，審試。

translations.literal: The edict replied: 'If Chong's son truly understands pitch in detail, distinguishes their kinship, and coordinates their sounds, examine him with care.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript answered: if the son really knows intervals, can sort families of notes, and can lock them in ensemble, test him rigorously—

sentences.zh: 不得依託父學，以聾為聰。

translations.literal: He may not rely on his father's learning and pretend deafness is acuity.
translations.idiomatic: —and do not let him hide behind his father's reputation.

sentences.zh: 聲微妙，獨非莫知，獨是莫曉。

translations.literal: The sound is subtle: only 'not-this' knows it, only 'this' understands it.
translations.idiomatic: Acoustics is subtle: outsiders never hear the fault, insiders alone notice the fit.

sentences.zh: 以律錯吹，能知命十二律不失一，乃為能傳崇學耳。

translations.literal: By muddling the pipes in blowing, only if he can name all twelve pitch commands without missing one may he be deemed able to transmit Chong's learning.'
translations.idiomatic: Have him blind-test the twelve pipes; only if he names every length without a slip may he inherit Yan Chong's chair.

sentences.zh: 」試宣十二律，其二中，其四不中，其六不知何律，宣遂罷。

translations.literal: Xuan was tested on the twelve pipes: two matched, four did not match, and six he could not identify; Xuan was therefore dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan flubbed the exam—two hits, four misses, six pipes he could not name—so the court sent him home.

sentences.zh: 自此律家莫能為准。

translations.literal: From this time pitch specialists could not use the zhun.
translations.idiomatic: After that debacle nobody could credibly wield the zhun.

sentences.zh: 靈帝熹平六年，東觀召典律者太子舍人張光等問准意，光等不知，歸閱舊藏，乃得其器。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ling's Xiping sixth year, the Eastern Institute summoned pitch specialists including secretariat attendant Zhang Guang to ask about the meaning of the zhun; Guang and others did not know, returned to search old storerooms, and only then obtained the instrument.
translations.idiomatic: In Lingdi's Xiping 6 the Eastern Pavilion called Zhang Guang and other experts to explain the zhun; they confessed ignorance, ransacked the archives, and finally turned the hardware up.

sentences.zh: 形制如房書，猶不能定其弦緩急。

translations.literal: Its form matched what Fang's text described, yet still they could not settle how tight or slack the strings should be.
translations.idiomatic: It looked exactly like Fang's drawing, yet they still could not agree how taut each string should be.

sentences.zh: 音，不可書以曉人，知之者欲教而無從，心達者體知而無師，故史官能辨清濁者遂絕。

translations.literal: Sound cannot be written to make another understand; those who know wish to teach but have no way, those whose minds grasp it understand in the body but have no teacher—so clerks who could distinguish clear and mud finally died out.
translations.idiomatic: Tone refuses to live on paper: masters who know cannot lecture it, savants who feel it cannot copy it—so the last archivists who could hear clean from muddy simply disappeared.

sentences.zh: 其可以相傳者，唯候氣而已。

translations.literal: What could still be handed down was only the ash-tube breath test.
translations.idiomatic: All that survived as a teachable rite was the ash-in-jar solstice test.

sentences.zh: 漢末紛亂，亡失雅樂。

translations.literal: At the end of Han turmoil prevailed, and refined court music was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Han collapsed, courtly "ya" music went missing in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 魏武時，河南杜夔精識音韻，為雅樂郎中，令鑄銅工柴玉鑄鐘，其聲均清濁多不如法，數毀改作，玉甚厭之，謂夔清濁任意，更相訴白于魏武王。

translations.literal: Under Cao Cao, Du Kui of Henan, who keenly understood tone color, served as gentleman for refined music; he ordered the bell-founder Chai Yu to cast bronze bells whose notes in clear and mud mostly violated the rule; time after time they were smashed and recast; Yu greatly resented it, claiming Kui set clear and mud at whim, and they went on lodging mutual accusations before Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's court relied on Du Kui of Henan, a connoisseur of timbre, as gentleman of ya music; Du told the founder Chai Yu to cast ritual bells, but the bronze kept missing the thirds rule and had to be smashed and remelted until Chai accused Du of arbitrary tuning and both men appealed to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 魏武王取玉所鑄鐘雜錯更試，然後知夔為精，於是罪玉。

translations.literal: Prince Wei took the bells Yu had cast, jumbled and tested them again, then understood that Kui was precise; thereupon Yu was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao personally shuffled Chai's bells back into the set, listened again, and decided Du had been right all along—Chai paid for the false accusation.

sentences.zh: 泰始十年，中書監荀勖、中書令張華出禦府銅竹律二十五具，部太樂郎劉秀等校試，其三具與杜夔及左延年律法同，其二十二具，視其銘題尺寸，是笛律也。

translations.literal: In Taishi ten, Palace Secretariat Supervisor Xun Xi and Palace Secretariat Director Zhang Hua brought out twenty-five bronze and bamboo pitch items from the imperial treasury, assigning Court Gentleman Liu Xiu of the Grand Music office to test them: three matched Du Kui's and Zuo Yanian's pitch law, while twenty-two, judging by their inscriptions of size, were flute templates.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Wudi's Taishi 10 Xun Xi and Zhang Hua hauled twenty-five bronze and bamboo measures from the palace vault for Liu Xiu to audition: three matched Du Kui and Zuo Yanian's law, while twenty-two bore flute dimensions carved on the shank.

sentences.zh: 問協律中郎將列和，辭：「昔魏明帝時，令和承受笛聲以作此律，欲使學者別居一坊，歌詠講習，依此律調。

translations.literal: They questioned harmonizer general Lie He, who replied: 'In Emperor Ming's Wei reign, He was ordered to take the flute's notes to make these templates, wishing to have students live in a separate ward singing and studying according to this tuning.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed General Lie He, who said Emperor Ming of Wei once told him to derive the pitch set from flute fingerings and house students in a separate compound to practice songs to those fingerings.

sentences.zh: 至於都合樂時，但識其尺寸之名，則絲竹歌詠，皆得均合。

translations.literal: When assembling the full orchestra one need only know the size labels, and strings, bamboo, and voices all could be matched evenly.
translations.idiomatic: In full ensemble you only read the length labels and every string, pipe, and voice lines up.

sentences.zh: 歌聲濁者用長笛長律，歌聲清者用短笛短律。

translations.literal: For muddy voices use long flute and long pipe; for clear voices use short flute and short pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Dark voices take the long bore; bright voices take the short.

sentences.zh: 凡弦歌調張清濁之制，不依笛尺寸名之，則不可知也。」

translations.literal: Where string-song tuning sets the rule for clear and mud, if one does not rely on the flute's size labels, it cannot be known.'
translations.idiomatic: Anyone tuning zithers or voices without those flute marks is working blind.

sentences.zh: 勖等奏：「昔先王之作樂也，以振風蕩俗，饗神祐賢，必協律呂之和，以節八音之中。

translations.literal: Xun Xi and others memorialized: 'When former kings made music, it was to stir wind and move custom, feast spirits and bless the worthy; they had to match the harmony of pitch pipes to moderate the middles of the eight timbres.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xi answered with a long memorial: the sages invented music to move wind and custom, to feed spirits and honor worthies, and they always locked the eight timbres to the twelve pipes.

sentences.zh: 是故郊祀朝宴，用之有制，歌奏分獻，清濁有宜。

translations.literal: Therefore suburban sacrifices and court banquets use them with set rules, song and offering divide cups, clear and mud each has its proper scale.
translations.idiomatic: Hence suburban rites and palace feasts follow fixed registers—anthem and libation each get their own cup, bright and dark ranges stay distinct.

sentences.zh: 故曰「五聲、十二律還相為宮」，此經傳記籍可得知者也。

translations.literal: Hence it is said, "Five sounds, twelve pipes cyclically become gong"—this is what can be learned from the classics and transmitted records.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the classics repeat that the five degrees and twelve tubes "take turns as gong."

sentences.zh: 如和對辭，笛之長短無所象則，率意而作，不由曲度。

translations.literal: According to He's reply, the flute's lengths have nothing they pattern on; they are made at whim and do not follow musical measure.
translations.idiomatic: Lie He's own confession is that his flutes follow no canonical length—they are guesswork, not measure.

sentences.zh: 考以正律，皆不相應；

translations.literal: Tested against orthodox pitch, none of them answers;
translations.idiomatic: Set them against the bronze pipes and none lines up;

sentences.zh: 吹其聲均，多不諧合。

translations.literal: blown, their tones average but mostly do not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: blow them and the averages sound smooth yet refuse to lock with the orchestra.

sentences.zh: 又辭'先師傳笛，別其清濁，直以長短。

translations.literal: He also said in reply, "Past masters passed down flutes, distinguishing clear and mud solely by length.
translations.idiomatic: He also admitted that teachers "passed flutes down" by cutting longer or shorter tubes—

sentences.zh: 工人裁制，舊不依律。

translations.literal: Craftsmen cutting them have never followed the pipes.'
translations.idiomatic: —and workshop cutters never used the pitch law at all.

sentences.zh: '是為作笛無法。

translations.literal: This means making flutes by no method.
translations.idiomatic: In other words, there was no method.

sentences.zh: 而和寫笛造律，又令琴瑟歌詠，從之為正，非所以稽古先哲，垂憲於後者也。

translations.literal: Yet He took flutes to write pitches and further made zithers and se and songs follow that as standard, which is not the way to examine antiquity or hand down models to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from those flutes he wrote the nominal pitches and forced zithers, se, and singers to obey—hardly the way to honor antiquity or leave a pattern for later kings.

sentences.zh: 謹條牒諸律，問和意狀如左。

translations.literal: We respectfully list each pitch and question He on the facts as at left.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore tabulate every pipe and put He's claims to the test point by point.

sentences.zh: 及依典制，用十二律造笛象十二枚，聲均調和，器用便利。

translations.literal: Following the classical code, we made twelve flutes modeled on the twelve pipes—twelve pieces whose sounds even out and whose instruments prove handy.
translations.idiomatic: Following the classics we bored twelve bamboo flutes, one for each pipe; they tune evenly and are easy to play.

sentences.zh: 講肄彈擊，必合律呂，況乎宴饗萬國，奏之廟堂者哉？

translations.literal: For lectures, plucking, and striking they are sure to match pitch pipes—how much more when feasting the myriad states and performing in the ancestral hall?
translations.idiomatic: If they hold for lessons and chamber music, they will surely hold when the feudatories banquet or the temple orchestra plays.

sentences.zh: 雖伶夔曠遠，至音難精，猶宜儀形古昔，以求厥衷，合乎經禮，於制為詳。

translations.literal: Though Ling Lun is far away and ultimate tone is hard to perfect, one should still take shape from antiquity to seek its inner mean, conforming to the classics and rites, which is thorough in regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Lun is millennia gone and perfection is elusive, yet the court should still mimic the old forms, seek the middle course, and hew to canonical ritual—that is the thorough path.

sentences.zh: 若可施用，請更部笛工選竹造作，下太樂樂府施行。

translations.literal: If this may be applied, please further assign flute craftsmen to select bamboo and fabricate, and promulgate through the Grand Music office.
translations.idiomatic: If the plan stands, commission bamboo cutters, build the set, and issue it through the Grand Music bureau.

sentences.zh: 平議諸杜夔、左延年律可皆留，其禦府笛正聲、下徽各一具，皆銘題作者姓名，其餘無所施用，還付禦府毀。

translations.literal: Collegially decide: Du Kui's and Zuo Yanian's pitches may all be kept; of the imperial-store flutes keep one correct-tone and one lower-zhi each, all inscribed with the maker's name; the rest, having no use, return to the treasury for destruction.'
translations.idiomatic: The collegial verdict: keep every pitch template by Du Kui and Zuo Yanian; from the palace flutes retain only one standard-length and one lower-register instrument, each stamped with its maker; melt the useless remainder back at the vault.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 勖又問和：「作笛為可依十二律作十二笛，令一孔依一律，然後乃以為樂不？

translations.literal: Xun Xi further asked He: 'In making flutes, should one rely on the twelve pipes to make twelve flutes, letting each hole answer one pitch, and only then deem the music correct?'
translations.idiomatic: Xun pressed again: must twelve holes on twelve tubes—one hole per pipe—be the definition of correct music?

sentences.zh: 」和辭：「太樂東廂長笛正聲已長四尺二寸，今當復取其下征之聲。

translations.literal: He replied: 'The grand music office's eastern-gallery long flute for correct tone is already four chi two cun long; now we would again take its lower-zhi tone.
translations.idiomatic: Lie answered that the eastern-gallery concert flute is already four chǐ two cùn, yet the court now wants its subdominant register as well.

sentences.zh: 於法，聲濁者笛當長，計其尺寸乃五尺有餘，和昔日作之，不可吹也。

translations.literal: By rule a muddy-tone flute should be long; reckoning its size comes to over five chi—what I once made could not be blown.'
translations.idiomatic: A dull register demands a longer bore—over five chǐ by the math—and the prototype I once cut could not be blown at all.

sentences.zh: 又，笛諸孔雖不校試，意謂不能得一孔輒應一律也。

translations.literal: 'Again, although the flute's holes were never tested, I suppose one cannot have each hole answer a single pitch at will.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, he said, without empirical tests you cannot expect every finger hole to land on a separate pipe tone.

sentences.zh: 」案太樂四尺二寸笛正聲均應蕤賓，以十二律還相為宮，推法下征之孔當應律大呂。

translations.literal: Checking: the grand music four-chi-two-cun flute's correct tone on average answers Ruíbīn; by the twelve pipes cyclically becoming gong, the hole for lower-zhi on the method should answer Dàlǚ.
translations.idiomatic: Auditors replied: the four-chi-two concert flute centers on Ruíbīn; if you rotate the twelve pipes as temporary gong, the lower-zhi vent should answer Dàlǚ.

sentences.zh: 大呂笛長二尺六寸有奇，不得長五尺餘。

translations.literal: A Dàlǚ flute is a little over two chi six cun long; it cannot be over five chi.
translations.idiomatic: A Dàlǚ bore is only a little past two chǐ six cùn—nowhere near five.

sentences.zh: 輒令太樂郎劉秀、鄧昊等依律作大呂笛以示和，又吹七律，一孔一校，聲皆相應。

translations.literal: The court therefore ordered Court Gentlemen Liu Xiu and Deng Hao to make a Dàlǚ flute by the pipes to show He, then blew the seven pitches, one hole tested at a time, and every note answered.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told Liu Xiu and Deng Hao to cut a Dàlǚ flute to spec, then pipe the seven degrees hole by hole—each matched the law.

sentences.zh: 然後令郝生鼓箏，宋同吹笛，以為雜引、《相和》諸曲。

translations.literal: Then they had Hao Sheng pluck the zheng and Song Tong blow the flute on assorted introductions and the 'Xianghe' suite pieces.
translations.idiomatic: They paired Hao Sheng's zheng with Song Tong's flute on preludes and the "Harmony" suites.

sentences.zh: 和乃辭曰：「自和父祖漢世以來，笛家相傳，不知此法，而令調均與律相應，實非所及也。

translations.literal: He then demurred: 'Since my father's and grandfather's generations in Han, flute masters have passed things down without knowing this method, yet you make tuning even and matching the pipes—truly beyond my reach.'
translations.idiomatic: Lie He finally conceded that Han-era flute families had never heard of such precision, yet the new instruments sang dead true—beyond anything he could match.

sentences.zh: 」郝生、魯基、種整、硃夏皆與和同。

translations.literal: Hao Sheng, Lu Ji, Zhong Zheng, and Zhu Xia all agreed with He.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Sheng, Lu Ji, Zhong Zheng, and Zhu Xia sided with Lie He.

sentences.zh: 又問和：「笛有六孔，及其體中之空為七，和為能盡名其宮商角徵不？

translations.literal: They further asked He: 'The flute has six holes plus the hollow in its body making seven—can you fully name their gong, shang, jue, and zhi?
translations.idiomatic: The board asked whether he could even name gong, shang, jue, and zhǐ for the six holes plus the bore.

sentences.zh: 孔調與不調，以何檢知？

translations.literal: For holes in tune or out of tune, by what do you test?'
translations.idiomatic: And how would he prove each vent was in tune?

sentences.zh: 」和辭：「先師相傳，吹笛但以作曲，相語為某曲當舉某指，初不知七孔盡應何聲也。

translations.literal: He replied: 'What past masters passed down was that to play the flute you only compose pieces, telling each other "this piece should lift such a finger"—at first they had no idea what sound each of the seven openings answered.'
translations.idiomatic: Lie admitted masters only traded finger charts—"lift the third finger here"—with no theory tying each hole to a pitch name.

sentences.zh: 若當作笛，其仰尚方笛工依案舊像訖，但吹取鳴者，初不復校其諸孔調與不調也。

translations.literal: If one is to make a flute, the Palace workshop craftsmen follow the old pattern and stop at blowing until it rings, never again checking whether the holes are in tune or not.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial flute makers still copy the old outline and quit as soon as the tube whistles, never calibrating the holes.

sentences.zh: 」案《周禮》調樂金石，有一定之聲，是故造鐘磬者先依律調之，然後施於廂懸。

translations.literal: Checking the 'Rites of Zhou': tuning metal and stone instruments has fixed sounds, so those who cast bells and chimes first tune them to the pipes before hanging them in the galleries.
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" says bronze and stone must be tuned to fixed pitches before they hang in the bell galleries.

sentences.zh: 作樂之時，諸音皆受鐘磬之均，即為悉應律也。

translations.literal: When making music, every timbre receives the evenness of bells and chimes, meaning all answer the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In performance every color listens back to the bells and chimes, which means everything is tied to the twelve pipes.

sentences.zh: 至於饗宴殿堂之上，無廂懸鐘磬，以笛有一定調，故諸弦歌皆從笛為正，是為笛猶鐘磬，宜必合於律呂。

translations.literal: When feasting in the main hall without gallery-hung bells and chimes, because the flute has one fixed tuning, all strings and songs take the flute as standard—thus the flute stands like bells and chimes and ought to agree with pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet hall lacks suspended bells, the flute becomes the temporary standard: strings and singers follow it exactly as they would follow the gallery chimes—so that lone bamboo must still obey the twelve pipes.

sentences.zh: 如和所對，直以意造，率短一寸，七孔聲均，不知其皆應何律，調與不調，無以檢正，唯取竹之鳴者，為無法制。

translations.literal: According to He's reply, he simply followed whim in construction, generally shortening one cun; the seven holes sound even, yet he does not know what pitch each answers, and for in-tune or out-of-tune there is no means of correction—only taking bamboo that will whistle is to make music with no method.
translations.idiomatic: Lie He's method amounts to shaving every tube roughly a cun short, drilling seven even holes, and never checking which pipe each hole should speak—if it blows, he ships it. That is not a method at all.

sentences.zh: 輒部郎劉秀、鄧昊、王豔、魏邵等與笛工參共作笛，工人造其形，律者定其聲，然後器象有制，音均和協。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gentlemen Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, Wang Yan, Wei Shao, and others jointly made flutes with the flute craftsmen: the workers shaped the body, the pitch specialists fixed the notes—only then did the instruments have regulation and the tones even and cooperative.
translations.idiomatic: The court then paired Liu Xiu, Deng Hao, Wang Yan, and Wei Shao with palace flute makers: carpenters cut the bamboo while acousticians set the scale, so each tube had both proper form and true pitch.

sentences.zh: 又問和：「若不知律呂之義作樂，音均高下清濁之調，當以何名之？

translations.literal: They further asked He: 'If one makes music without understanding the meaning of pitch pipes, by what name should one call the regulation of higher and lower, clear and muddy?'
translations.idiomatic: They pressed Lie He again: without knowing what the twelve pipes mean, what name could you give to "bright" or "dark" tuning?

sentences.zh: 」和辭：「每合樂時，隨歌者聲之清濁，用笛有長短。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Whenever assembling music, following the singer's clear or muddy voice, one uses flutes long or short.
translations.idiomatic: Lie said the band simply grabbed a longer or shorter flute to match the vocalist.

sentences.zh: 假令聲濁者用三尺二笛，因名曰此三尺二調也；

translations.literal: Suppose the voice is muddy: use a three-chi-two-cun flute and therefore call it the three-chi-two tuning;
translations.idiomatic: A thick voice gets a three-chi-two tube, and everyone nicknames that gauge "the three-chi-two mode";

sentences.zh: 聲清者用二尺九笛，因名曰此二尺九調也。

translations.literal: if the voice is clear, use a two-chi-nine-cun flute and therefore call it the two-chi-nine tuning.
translations.idiomatic: a bright voice gets a two-chi-nine tube, nicknamed "the two-chi-nine mode."

sentences.zh: 漢魏相傳，施行皆然。

translations.literal: Han and Wei handed this down and practiced it in every case.'
translations.idiomatic: That folk habit, he claimed, ran unchanged from Han through Wei.

sentences.zh: 」案《周禮》奏六樂，乃奏黃鐘，歌大呂；

translations.literal: Checking the 'Rites of Zhou': in performing the six great musics, one then plays Yellow Bell and sings Great Regulator;
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" orders the six suites as "sound Yellow Bell, sing Dàlǚ";

sentences.zh: 乃奏太蔟，歌應鐘，皆以律呂之義，紀歌奏清濁。

translations.literal: then plays Tàicù and sings Bell of Response—all by the meaning of pitch pipes, recording clear and muddy for song and accompaniment.
translations.idiomatic: then "sound Tàicù, sing Yìngzhōng"—every pairing is named from the pipes, not from bamboo lengths.

sentences.zh: 而和所稱以二尺，三尺為名，雖漢魏用之，俗而不典。

translations.literal: Yet what He calls naming by two chi or three chi, although Han and Wei used it, is vulgar and not canonical.
translations.idiomatic: Lie He's foot-and-inch nicknames may have been common, but they are not canonical nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 部郎劉秀、鄧昊等以律作笛，三尺二寸者應無射之律，若宜用長笛，執樂者曰請奏無射；

translations.literal: Gentlemen Liu Xiu and Deng Hao, making flutes by the pipes, find that three chi two cun answers the Wúyì pitch; if a long flute is appropriate, the conductor says, 'Please sound Wúyì.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu's team shows that a three-chi-two tube matches Wúyì, so the director can honestly call, "Play Wúyì" when the chart demands the long pipe;

sentences.zh: 二尺八寸四分四厘應黃鐘之律，若宜用短笛，執樂者曰請奏黃鐘。

translations.literal: two chi eight cun four fen four li answers Yellow Bell; if a short flute is appropriate, the conductor says, 'Please sound Yellow Bell.'
translations.idiomatic: while two chǐ eight cùn four fēn four lí matches Yellow Bell, so the call becomes "Play Yellow Bell" when the short bore is needed.

sentences.zh: 則歌奏之義，若合經禮，考之古典，於制為雅。

translations.literal: Then the meaning of song and accompaniment, if it matches the classics and rites, examined against ancient models, is refined in regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Song and accompaniment named that way line up with the ritual classics—exactly the elegant usage the canon expects.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「予欲聞六律、五聲、八音，在治忽。

translations.literal: The 'Canon of Documents' says: 'I wish to hear the six pipes, the five timbres, and the eight kinds of sound—in order and confusion among the governed.'
translations.idiomatic: The "Canon of Documents" says Shun wanted "the six pipes, the five notes, and the eight timbres"—the acoustic mirror of good and bad government.

sentences.zh: 」《周禮》、《國語》載六律六同，《禮記》又曰「五聲、十二律還相為宮」。

translations.literal: The 'Rites of Zhou' and 'Discourses of the States' record the six pipes and six 'tongs'; the 'Record of Rites' again says 'five timbres, twelve pipes cyclically become gong.'
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" and "Discourses of the States" pair six lǜ with six tóng; the "Record of Rites" repeats that five voices and twelve tubes rotate as gong.

sentences.zh: 劉歆、班固撰《律曆志》亦紀十二律，惟京房始創六十律。

translations.literal: Liu Xin and Ban Gu, composing the 'Treatise on Pitch and Calendar,' likewise recorded the twelve pipes; only Jing Fang first created the sixty pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin and Ban Gu's monograph still tracks twelve pipes; Jing Fang alone extended the cycle to sixty.

sentences.zh: 至章帝時，其法己絕，蔡邕追紀其言，亦曰今無能為者。

translations.literal: By Emperor Zhang's time its method was already cut off; Cai Yong later recorded his words, also saying none today can practice it.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhangdi's reign the sixtyfold art was dead; Cai Yong copied Jing Fang's boast yet admitted no living master could rebuild it.

sentences.zh: 依案古典及今音家所用，六十律者無施于樂。

translations.literal: Checking classical models and what modern acousticians use, the sixty pipes have no application in performance.
translations.idiomatic: Between ancient manuals and modern orchestras, the sixty mutations never reach the stage.

sentences.zh: 謹依典記，以五聲、十二律還相為宮之法，制十二笛象，記注圖側，如別，省圖，不如視笛之孔，故復重作蕤賓伏孔笛。

translations.literal: Respectfully following canonical records, using the method of five timbres and twelve pipes cyclically becoming gong, we fashioned twelve flute models, with annotations at the margins of the diagram, separately submitted; because viewing the diagram is inferior to viewing the flute's holes, we further made a Ruibīn stopped-hole flute.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore built twelve demonstration flutes keyed to the classical "five over twelve" cycle, sketched them with marginal notes, and—because ink diagrams mislead the eye—recut a Ruibīn flute with its muted vent to show the holes directly.

sentences.zh: 其制云：

translations.literal: Its specifications read:
translations.idiomatic: The specifications run as follows:

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之笛，正聲應黃鐘，下徵應林鐘，長二尺八寸四分四厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell flute: correct tone answers Yellow Bell, lower zhi answers Forest Bell, length two chi eight cun four fen four li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell tube's concert register centers on Yellow Bell, its subdominant on Forest Bell, and its sounding length is two chǐ eight cùn four fēn four lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 正聲調法，以黃鐘為宮，則姑洗為角，翕笛之聲應姑洗，故以四角之長為黃鐘之笛也。

translations.literal: Correct-tone regulation method: with Yellow Bell as gong, Gǔxǐ is jue; the stopped flute's tone answers Gǔxǐ, therefore take the four-corner length as the Yellow Bell flute.
translations.idiomatic: In concert tuning, Yellow Bell is gong and Gǔxǐ is jue; the half-stopped bore must speak Gǔxǐ, so the tube's length equals the sum of the Yellow Bell and Gǔxǐ pipe lengths measured from the mouth end.

sentences.zh: 其宮聲正而不倍，故曰正聲。

translations.literal: Its gong note is true and not doubled, therefore it is called correct tone.
translations.idiomatic: Because the fundamental is neither doubled nor halved, musicians call this register the "true" or concert pitch.

sentences.zh: 正聲調法：黃鐘為宮，第一孔也。

translations.literal: Correct-tone regulation method: Yellow Bell is gong—the first hole.
translations.idiomatic: Hole one, counting from the mouth, is gong on Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 應鐘為變宮，第二孔也。

translations.literal: Bell of Response is altered gong—the second hole.
translations.idiomatic: Hole two is the altered gong on Yìngzhōng.

sentences.zh: 南呂為羽，第三孔也。

translations.literal: Southern Regulator is yu—the third hole.
translations.idiomatic: Hole three is yu on Nánlǚ.

sentences.zh: 林鐘為徵，第四孔也。

translations.literal: Forest Bell is zhi—the fourth hole.
translations.idiomatic: Hole four is zhǐ on Línzhōng.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓為變徵，第五附孔也。

translations.literal: Ruibīn is altered zhi—the fifth auxiliary hole.
translations.idiomatic: Ruibīn's altered zhǐ sits on the fifth side hole.

sentences.zh: 姑洗為角，笛體中聲。

translations.literal: Gǔxǐ is jue—the tone inside the flute body.
translations.idiomatic: Gǔxǐ's jue sounds from the air column inside the bore.

sentences.zh: 太蔟為商。

translations.literal: Tàicù is shang—the rear outlet hole.
translations.idiomatic: Tàicù's shang vents through the hole behind the player's hands.

sentences.zh: 笛後出孔也。

translations.literal: The shang note is muddier than jue and ought to lie below jue, but because jue's voice sits inside the body, the shang hole is raised above gong so that it is clearer than gong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang should sit lower than jue, yet jue lives inside the tube, so the shang vent is punched above gong to keep it brighter than the fundamental.

sentences.zh: 商聲濁於角，當在角下，而角聲以在體中，故上其商孔，令在宮上，清于宮也。

translations.literal: Thus gong and shang are true; the remaining notes are all doubled generations;
translations.idiomatic: Gong and shang stay on the true pipe; every other step borrows an octave duplicate;

sentences.zh: 然則宮商正也，餘聲皆倍也；

translations.literal: therefore from gong downward, each hole moved downward becomes muddier.
translations.idiomatic: so each hole farther from the mouth sounds duller than the last.

sentences.zh: 是故從宮以下，孔轉下轉濁也。

translations.literal: This section records the names of the flute holes in top-to-bottom order.
translations.idiomatic: This passage only names the holes from crown to foot.

sentences.zh: 此章記笛孔上下次第之名也。

translations.literal: The next section explains mutual generation of pitch pipes—the system of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: The following section explains how the pipes beget one another—the geometry of the flute.

sentences.zh: 下章說律呂相生，笛之制也。

translations.literal: Correct-tone regulation method: Yellow Bell is gong.
translations.idiomatic: Concert method again: Yellow Bell on gong.

sentences.zh: 正聲調法，黃鐘為宮。

translations.literal: To make the Yellow Bell flute and seek the gong hole, take the Gǔxǐ and Yellow Bell pipe lengths, measure down from the flute head; exhausting the combined length of the two pipes to make a hole yields the gong tone.
translations.idiomatic: Mark gong by measuring from the blowing edge the combined lengths of the Gǔxǐ and Yellow Bell tubes; where that tally ends, drill gong.

sentences.zh: 作黃鐘之笛，將求宮孔，以始洗及黃鐘律，從笛首下度之，盡二律之長而為孔，則得宮聲也。

translations.literal: Gong begets zhi: Yellow Bell begets Forest Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Gong generates zhǐ, so Yellow Bell spawns Forest Bell.

sentences.zh: 宮生徵，黃鐘生林鐘也。

translations.literal: Take the Forest Bell pipe measure downward from the gong hole.
translations.idiomatic: Drop the Forest Bell length below the gong vent.

sentences.zh: 以林鐘之律從宮孔下度之。

translations.literal: Exhausting the pipe measure to make a hole yields the zhi tone.
translations.idiomatic: Drill zhǐ where that measurement stops.

sentences.zh: 盡律作孔，則得徵聲也。

translations.literal: Zhi begets shang: Forest Bell begets Tàicù.
translations.idiomatic: Zhǐ generates shang, so Forest Bell spawns Tàicù.

sentences.zh: 徵生商，林鐘生太蔟也。

translations.literal: Take the Tàicù pipe measure upward from the zhi hole; exhausting the pipe to make a hole yields the shang tone.
translations.idiomatic: Measure up from the zhǐ hole by the Tàicù length; the next stop is shang.

sentences.zh: 乙太蔟律從徵孔上度之，盡律以為孔，則得商聲也。

translations.literal: Shang begets yu: Tàicù begets Southern Regulator.
translations.idiomatic: Shang generates yu, so Tàicù spawns Nánlǚ.

sentences.zh: 商生羽，太蔟生南呂也。

translations.literal: Take the Southern Regulator pipe measure downward from the shang hole; exhausting the pipe to make a hole yields the yu tone.
translations.idiomatic: Down from shang by the Nánlǚ length comes yu.

sentences.zh: 以南呂律從商孔下度之，盡律為孔，則得羽聲也。

translations.literal: Yu begets jue: Southern Regulator begets Gǔxǐ.
