translations.idiomatic: Yu generates jue, so Nánlǚ spawns Gǔxǐ.

sentences.zh: 羽生角，南呂生姑洗也。

translations.literal: Take the Gǔxǐ pipe measure upward from the yu hole; exhausting the pipe to make a hole yields the jue tone.
translations.idiomatic: Up from yu by the Gǔxǐ length lands jue.

sentences.zh: 以姑洗律從羽孔上行度之，盡律而為孔，則得角聲也。

translations.literal: Yet that would emerge above the shang hole, beyond the left hand's reach of the flutist.
translations.idiomatic: That point would sit above the shang hole—where the player's left hand cannot reach.

sentences.zh: 然則出於商孔之上，吹笛者左手所不及也。

translations.literal: Measuring downward from the yu hole, exhausting the pipe to make a hole also yields jue, emerging below the auxiliary shang hole—beyond the right hand's reach—therefore no jue hole is cut.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring down from yu by the same length also yields jue, but the vent would fall under the thumb hole where the right hand cannot cover it, so no separate jue hole is bored.

sentences.zh: 從羽孔下行度之，盡律而為孔，亦得角聲，出於商附孔之下，則吹者右手所不逮也，故不作角孔。

translations.literal: Extrapolating downward and again doubling the evenness, therefore the jue tone resides inside the flute body—this is the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: Doubling the air column downward parks jue inside the bore—exactly the classical layout.

sentences.zh: 推而下之，復倍其均，是以角聲在笛體中，古之制也。

translations.literal: The old acousticians' method, although doubling once or twice, only requires the evenness to match, sufficient for answering and leading voices, without harming the overall tuning of the piece.
translations.idiomatic: Older masters doubled or halved lengths freely as long as ensemble balance held, because duets only need matching color, not a fresh hole for every partial.

sentences.zh: 音家舊法，雖一倍再倍，但令均同，適足為唱和之聲，無害于曲均故也。

translations.literal: The 'Discourses of the States' says gourd and bamboo 'profit from regulation and consult convenience,' meaning they should follow practical use and yield to what is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The "Discourses" line that gourd and bamboo "yield to fit and follow convenience" means just this: build what the band can actually finger.

sentences.zh: 《國語》曰，匏竹利制，議宜，謂便於事用從宜者也。

translations.literal: Jue begets altered gong: Gǔxǐ begets Bell of Response.
translations.idiomatic: Jue spawns altered gong, so Gǔxǐ leads to Yìngzhōng.

sentences.zh: 角生變宮，姑洗生應鐘也。

translations.literal: The so-called place that ought to be a jue hole but emerges above shang is marked with an ink dot according to the Bell of Response pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Where theory wants a jue hole above shang, draftsmen ink a dot sized to the Yìngzhōng length.

sentences.zh: 上句所謂當為角孔而出於商上者，墨點識之，以應鐘律。

translations.literal: Measuring downward from this dot, exhausting the pipe to make a hole yields the altered-gong tone.
translations.idiomatic: Drill downward from that dot by the Yìngzhōng pipe and you capture altered gong.

sentences.zh: 從此點下行度之，盡律為孔，則得變宮之聲也。

translations.literal: Altered gong begets altered zhi: Bell of Response begets Ruibīn.
translations.idiomatic: Altered gong leads to altered zhǐ, Yìngzhōng to Ruibīn.

sentences.zh: 變宮生變徵，應鐘生蕤賓也。

translations.literal: Take the Ruibīn pipe measure downward from altered gong; exhausting the pipe to make a hole yields the altered-zhi tone.
translations.idiomatic: Drop the Ruibīn length from altered gong to locate altered zhǐ.

sentences.zh: 以蕤賓律從變宮下度之，盡律為孔，則得變征之聲。

translations.literal: The system of the twelve flutes: each takes its own gong as lord; the mutual-generation method, whether doubling or halving, for convenient use follows one pattern throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the twelve model flutes uses its namesake as temporary gong; whether you double or halve lengths, the workshop rule stays the same.

sentences.zh: 十二笛之制，各以其宮為主，相生之法，或倍或半，其便事用，例皆一也。

translations.literal: Lower-zhi regulation method: Forest Bell is gong—the fourth hole.
translations.idiomatic: Subdominant tuning makes Forest Bell gong on the fourth hole.

sentences.zh: 下徵調法：林鐘為宮，第四孔也。

translations.literal: Originally the zhi of correct-tone Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: That hole was zhǐ in the concert Yellow Bell chart.

sentences.zh: 本正聲黃鐘之徵。

translations.literal: Zhi is clearer than gong and ought to lie above gong; for convenience on the flute one doubles it downward to make it muddy, therefore it is called lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: True zhǐ should sit above gong, but the flute doubles it down an octave for ergonomics, so players call the mode "lower zhǐ."

sentences.zh: 徵清，當在宮上，用笛之宜，倍令濁下，故曰下徵。

translations.literal: Lower zhi again serving as gong is what the 'Record' calls 'five timbres, twelve pipes cyclically become gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Letting that lowered zhǐ rotate into gong is precisely the "five notes, twelve tubes take turns as gong" rule from the "Record of Rites."

sentences.zh: 下徵更為宮者，《記》所謂「五聲，十二律還相為宮」也。

translations.literal: Thus correct tone is clear, lower zhi is muddy.
translations.idiomatic: Concert pitch stays bright; the lowered mode is the darker twin.

sentences.zh: 然則正聲清，下徵為濁也。

translations.literal: Southern Regulator is shang—the third hole.
translations.idiomatic: Hole three becomes shang on Nánlǚ.

sentences.zh: 南呂為商，第三孔也。

translations.literal: Originally the yu of correct-tone Yellow Bell; now it is the shang of lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: It used to be yu in the concert chart; in lower zhǐ it is shang.

sentences.zh: 本正聲黃鐘之羽，今為下征之商也。

translations.literal: Bell of Response is jue—the second hole.
translations.idiomatic: Hole two is jue on Yìngzhōng.

sentences.zh: 應鐘為角，第二孔也。

translations.literal: Originally the altered gong of correct-tone Yellow Bell; now it is the jue of lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly altered gong in the concert set; now jue in the lowered set.

sentences.zh: 本正聲黃鐘之變宮，今為下征之角也。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is altered zhi; in lower-zhi mode Forest Bell is gong, and Dàlǚ ought to be altered zhi, yet the Yellow Bell flute has no Dàlǚ voice, so Yellow Bell is borrowed for altered zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lower zhǐ needs Dàlǚ as altered zhǐ while Forest Bell is gong, but the Yellow Bell bore has no Dàlǚ slot, so acousticians fake the step with Yellow Bell itself.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘為變徵，下征之調，林鐘為宮，大呂當為變徵，而黃鐘笛本無大呂之聲，故假用黃鐘以為變徵也。

translations.literal: In the borrowing method, to obtain the altered-zhi tone, open together the Yellow Bell, Tàicù, and Bell of Response holes.
translations.idiomatic: The trick is to lift Yellow Bell, Tàicù, and Yìngzhōng together when altered zhǐ is required.

sentences.zh: 假用之法，當為變征之聲，則俱髮黃鐘及太蔟、應鐘三孔。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell answers muddy while Tàicù is clear; the Dàlǚ pitch lies between the two pipes; opening all three holes and shading the tone between them yields the sound of Dàlǚ altered zhi (the received text is damaged at this phrase).
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell speaks dull, Tàicù bright; Dàlǚ lives between them. Half-covering all three vents and shading the airstream splits the difference, approximating Dàlǚ's altered zhǐ—though the manuscript is corrupt at the verb describing the embouchure.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘應濁而太蔟清，大呂律在二律之間，俱發三孔而徵磑蒦之，則得大呂變征之聲矣。

translations.literal: For all flutes in lower-zhi mode, the method of seeking altered zhi is like this.
translations.idiomatic: Every lower-zhǐ flute uses the same three-hole shading for its borrowed altered zhǐ.

sentences.zh: 諸笛下徵調求變征之法，皆如此也。

translations.literal: Tàicù is zhi—the rear outlet hole.
translations.idiomatic: Tàicù supplies zhǐ on the rear hole.

sentences.zh: 太蔟為徵，笛後出孔。

translations.literal: Originally the shang of correct tone; now it is the zhi of lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was shang in the concert chart; now zhǐ in the lowered chart.

sentences.zh: 本正聲之商，今為下征之徵也。

translations.literal: Gǔxǐ is yu—the absorbed tone inside the body.
translations.idiomatic: Gǔxǐ's yu rings from the stopped column inside the bore.

sentences.zh: 姑洗為羽，笛體中翕聲。

translations.literal: Originally the jue of correct tone; now it is the yu of lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was jue in the concert chart; now yu in the lowered chart.

sentences.zh: 本正聲之角，今為下征之羽。

translations.literal: Ruibīn is altered gong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruibīn hosts altered gong.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓為變宮。

translations.literal: That is the auxiliary hole.
translations.idiomatic: That is the side vent.

sentences.zh: 附孔是也。

translations.literal: Originally the altered zhi of correct tone; now it is the altered gong of lower zhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was altered zhǐ upstairs; downstairs it becomes altered gong.

sentences.zh: 本正聲之變徵也，今為下征之變宮也。

translations.literal: Thus in correct-tone mode holes moved downward grow muddier; in lower-zhi mode holes moved upward grow clearer.
translations.idiomatic: So concert tuning darkens as you march toward the foot, while lowered zhǐ brightens as you march back toward the crown.

sentences.zh: 然則正聲之調，孔轉下轉濁，下征之調，孔轉上轉清也。

translations.literal: Clear-jue mode: taking Gǔxǐ as gong means using the absorbed tone inside the body as gong.
translations.idiomatic: The "clear jue" recipe makes Gǔxǐ the temporary gong—that is, the stopped air column inside the tube.

sentences.zh: 清角之調：以姑洗為宮，即是笛體中翕聲。

translations.literal: Clear-jue mode: taking Gǔxǐ as gong means using the absorbed tone inside the flute body as gong.
translations.idiomatic: The "clear jue" key treats the stopped column inside the bore as temporary gong on Gǔxǐ.

sentences.zh: 于正聲為角，於下徵為羽。

translations.literal: For correct tone it is jue; for lower zhi it is yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the concert chart that column is jue; in the lowered-zhǐ chart it is yu.

sentences.zh: 清角之調乃以為宮，而哨吹令清，故曰清角。

translations.literal: Clear-jue mode takes that as gong and whistles the blowing to make it clear, therefore it is called clear jue.
translations.idiomatic: Players treat that column as gong and overblow it bright, which is why musicians call the mode "clear jue."

sentences.zh: 惟得為宛詩謠俗之曲，不合雅樂也。

translations.literal: It can only supply popular ditties and folk tunes, not refined ya music.
translations.idiomatic: It works for street songs and common airs, not for court ya music.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓為商，正也。

translations.literal: Ruibīn is shang—this is orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Ruibīn as shang is the canonical assignment.

sentences.zh: 林鐘為角，非正也。

translations.literal: Forest Bell is jue—this is not orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell as jue is already a compromise step.

sentences.zh: 南呂為變徵，非正也。

translations.literal: Southern Regulator is altered zhi—this is not orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Nánlǚ as altered zhǐ is another non-canonical rung.

sentences.zh: 應鐘為徵，正也。

translations.literal: Bell of Response is zhi—this is orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Yìngzhōng as the zhi degree is the proper assignment here.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘為羽，非正也。

translations.literal: Yellow Bell is yu—this is not orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell as yu is again an expedient, not the classical mapping.

sentences.zh: 太蔟為變宮。

translations.literal: Tàicù is altered gong.
translations.idiomatic: Tàicù supplies the altered gong step.

sentences.zh: 非正也。

translations.literal: Not orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Again, not a canonical pairing.

sentences.zh: 清角之調，唯宮、商及徵與律相應，餘四聲非正者皆濁，一律哨吹令清，假而用之，其例一也。

translations.literal: In clear-jue mode only gong, shang, and zhi answer the pitch pipes; the other four non-canonical voices are muddy, and each pipe must be whistled bright for borrowed use—the rule is the same in every case.
translations.idiomatic: Under the clear-jue key only gong, shang, and zhǐ lock to the bronze standard; the other four steps stay dark until a player overblows them into tune.

sentences.zh: 凡笛體用律，長者八之，蕤賓、林鐘也。

translations.literal: Whenever the flute body applies pitch lengths, the long cases multiply by eight—Ruibīn and Forest Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Long-chamber flutes scale by eight against the pipe length—Ruibīn and Forest Bell fall in that class.

sentences.zh: 短者四之。

translations.literal: The short cases multiply by four.
translations.idiomatic: Short chambers multiply by four instead.

sentences.zh: 其餘十笛，皆四角也。

translations.literal: The remaining ten flutes all use the corner (jue) multiplier.
translations.idiomatic: The other ten models all take the "corner" ratio as their yardstick.

sentences.zh: 空中實容，長者十六。

translations.literal: For the hollow's solid capacity, the long ones use sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Interior volume for the long set follows the sixteenfold rule.

sentences.zh: 短笛竹宜受八律之黍也。

translations.literal: Bamboo for short flutes should chamber the millet tally of eight pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Short-flute culms need a bore that holds eight pipes' worth of millet by measure.

sentences.zh: 若長短大小不合於此，或器用不便聲均法度之齊等也。

translations.literal: If length, shortness, or overall size do not match this, or the implement is awkward so that evenness of tone and metrical balance cannot be equal,
translations.idiomatic: If you ignore those ratios or pick clumsy bamboo, timbre and measure fall out of step,

sentences.zh: 然笛竹率上大下小，不能均齊，必不得已，取其聲均合。

translations.literal: yet flute bamboo is generally thick above and thin below, unable to be perfectly even; when unavoidable, take what yields even sound and matching.
translations.idiomatic: and real culms taper from fat crown to narrow foot—when theory and wood disagree, chase an even sound rather than perfect arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 三宮，一曰正聲，二曰下徵，三曰清角也。

translations.literal: The three modes are: first, correct tone; second, lower zhi; third, clear jue.
translations.idiomatic: The three usable modes are concert pitch, lowered zhǐ, and brightened jue.

sentences.zh: 二十一變也。

translations.literal: Twenty-one modulations.
translations.idiomatic: Together they yield twenty-one modulating steps.

sentences.zh: 宮有七聲，錯綜用之，故二十一變也。

translations.literal: Gong has seven degrees; woven together in use, therefore there are twenty-one mutations.
translations.idiomatic: Because gong carries seven usable degrees that can be permuted, the full set of modulations comes to twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 諸笛例皆一也。

translations.literal: All flutes follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Every flute model follows the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 伏孔四，所以便事用也。

translations.literal: There are four hidden holes, provided for convenience in performance.
translations.idiomatic: Four "buried" vents are cut for practical fingering.

sentences.zh: 一曰正角，出於商上者也，二曰倍角，近笛下者也，三曰變宮，近于宮孔，倍令下者也；

translations.literal: The first is called correct jue, emerging above shang; the second is doubled jue, set near the flute's foot; the third is altered gong, close to the gong hole, halved downward for convenience;
translations.idiomatic: First comes true jue venting above shang, then doubled jue down by the foot, then altered gong tucked beside the gong hole and dropped an octave—

sentences.zh: 四曰變徵，遠于徵孔，倍令高者也。

translations.literal: the fourth is called altered zhi, set farther from the zhi hole, doubled upward for height.
translations.idiomatic: and finally altered zhǐ offset beyond the zhǐ hole and raised an octave.

sentences.zh: 或倍或半，或四分一，取則於琴徽也。

translations.literal: Sometimes doubling, sometimes halving, sometimes taking one quarter—taking the zither's frets as their model.
translations.idiomatic: The offsets follow zither frets: double, half, or add a quarter—

sentences.zh: 四者皆不作其孔，而取其度，以應退上下之法，所以協聲均，便事用也。

translations.literal: All four do not receive a bored hole; they take only the measured distance to answer the rules of stepping back or upward, thereby harmonizing tones and easing performance.
translations.idiomatic: —without visible bores, only measured lengths that obey the up-and-down rules so the scale evens out and the hands stay nimble.

sentences.zh: 其本孔隱而不見，故曰伏孔也。

translations.literal: Their root holes are hidden and unseen, therefore they are called 'hidden holes.'
translations.idiomatic: Because those roots stay invisible, builders call them "hidden" vents.

sentences.zh: 大呂之笛，正聲應大呂，下徵應夷則，長二尺六寸六分三厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Dàlǚ flute: correct tone answers Dàlǚ, lower zhi answers Yízé, length two chi six cun six fen three li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Dàlǚ template answers Dàlǚ in concert pitch and Yízé in lowered zhǐ, with a tube of two chǐ six cùn six fēn three lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 太蔟之笛，正聲應太蔟，下徵應南呂，長二尺五寸三分一厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Tàicù flute: correct tone answers Tàicù, lower zhi answers Southern Regulator, length two chi five cun three fen one li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Tàicù pipe locks to Tàicù and Nánlǚ at two chǐ five cùn three fēn one lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 夾鐘之笛，正聲應夾鐘，下徵應無射，長二尺四寸。

translations.literal: The Jiázhōng flute: correct tone answers Jiázhōng, lower zhi answers Wúyì, length two chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiázhōng model answers Jiázhōng and Wúyì at two chǐ four cùn.

sentences.zh: 姑洗之笛，正聲應姑洗，下徵應應鐘，長二尺二寸三分三厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Gǔxǐ flute: correct tone answers Gǔxǐ, lower zhi answers Bell of Response, length two chi two cun three fen three li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Gǔxǐ flute answers Gǔxǐ and Yìngzhōng at two chǐ two cùn three fēn three lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之笛，正聲應蕤賓，下徵應大呂，長三尺九寸九分五厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Ruibīn flute: correct tone answers Ruibīn, lower zhi answers Dàlǚ, length three chi nine cun nine fen five li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Ruibīn bore answers Ruibīn and Dàlǚ at three chǐ nine cùn nine fēn five lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 變宮近宮孔，故倍半令下，便於用也。

translations.literal: Because altered gong sits near the gong hole, it is halved downward for ease of use.
translations.idiomatic: Altered gong hugs the main hole, so the pattern drops it an octave for the player's thumb.

sentences.zh: 林鐘亦如之一。

translations.literal: Forest Bell follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Forest Bell uses the same altered-gong trick.

sentences.zh: 林鐘之笛，正聲應林鐘，下徵應太蔟，長三尺七寸九分七厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Forest Bell flute: correct tone answers Forest Bell, lower zhi answers Tàicù, length three chi seven cun nine fen seven li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Forest Bell template answers Línzhōng and Tàicù at three chǐ seven cùn nine fēn seven lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 夷則之笛，正聲應夷則，下徵應夾鐘，長三盡六寸。

translations.literal: The Yízé flute: correct tone answers Yízé, lower zhi answers Jiázhōng, length three chi six cun (the manuscript reads 三盡六寸, emended to three chi six cun).
translations.idiomatic: The Yízé pipe answers Yízé and Jiázhōng; the received text's "three exhaust six cun" is emended to three chǐ six cùn.

sentences.zh: 變宮之法，亦如蕤賓，體用四角，故四分益一也。

translations.literal: The method for altered gong likewise follows Ruibīn: the body uses the corner length, therefore it adds one fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Altered gong on this flute copies Ruibīn's corner-length body, so the math adds a fourth.

sentences.zh: 南呂之笛，正聲應南呂，下徵姑洗，長三尺三寸七分有奇。

translations.literal: The Southern Regulator flute: correct tone answers Southern Regulator, lower zhi answers Gǔxǐ, length three chi three cun seven fen with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Nánlǚ model answers Nánlǚ and Gǔxǐ at three chǐ three cùn seven fēn plus a remainder (the line omits the usual "answers" verb before Gǔxǐ).

sentences.zh: 無射之笛，正聲應無射，下徵應中呂，長三尺二寸。

translations.literal: The Wúyì flute: correct tone answers Wúyì, lower zhi answers Zhònglǚ, length three chi two cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Wúyì bore answers Wúyì and Zhònglǚ at three chǐ two cùn.

sentences.zh: 應鐘之笛，正聲應應鐘，下徵應蕤賓，長二尺九寸九分六厘有奇。

translations.literal: The Bell of Response flute: correct tone answers Bell of Response, lower zhi answers Ruibīn, length two chi nine cun nine fen six li with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Yìngzhōng flute answers Yìngzhōng and Ruibīn at two chǐ nine cùn nine fēn six lí plus a remainder.

sentences.zh: 五音十二律

translations.literal: The five notes and twelve pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Five degrees and twelve classical pipes.

sentences.zh: 土音宮，數八十一，為聲之始。

translations.literal: Earth's timbre is gong; its number is eighty-one—the beginning of sound.
translations.idiomatic: The earth class is gong, tallied at eighty-one, where acoustics begins.

sentences.zh: 屬土者，以其最濁，君之象也。

translations.literal: What belongs to earth is the muddiest register, image of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Earth sounds stay darkest, like the sovereign's steady voice.

sentences.zh: 季夏之氣和，則宮聲調。

translations.literal: When the qi of late summer is harmonious, then the gong note is in tune.
translations.idiomatic: When the last month of summer's qi is balanced, gong rings true.

sentences.zh: 宮亂則荒，其君驕。

translations.literal: When gong is chaotic, then there is wasteland; its ruler is arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: When gong slips, the land feels empty and the king turns proud.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之宮，律最長也。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell gong has the longest pipe of all.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Bell's gong carries the longest tube in the set.

sentences.zh: 火音徵，三分宮去一以生，其數五十四。

translations.literal: Fire's timbre is zhi; from gong subtract one third to engender it; its number is fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The fire class is zhǐ, born by taking a third from gong, numbered fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 屬火者，以其徵清，事之象也。

translations.literal: What belongs to fire is that zhi is clear, image of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fire sounds are bright, like the busy work of government.

sentences.zh: 夏氣和，則徵聲調。

translations.literal: When summer's qi is harmonious, then the zhi note is in tune.
translations.idiomatic: When midsummer qi is balanced, zhǐ rings true.

sentences.zh: 徵亂則哀，其事勤也。

translations.literal: When zhi is chaotic, then there is lament; its tasks are toilsome.
translations.idiomatic: When zhǐ slips, music turns mournful and every task feels like drudgery.

sentences.zh: 金音商，三分徵益一以生，其數七十二。

translations.literal: Metal's timbre is shang; add one third to zhi to engender it; its number is seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Metal is shang, born by adding a third to zhǐ, numbered seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 屬金者，以其濁次宮，臣之象也。

translations.literal: What belongs to metal is that it is next muddier after gong, image of the minister.
translations.idiomatic: Metal sits just below gong in darkness, like the minister's supporting voice.

sentences.zh: 秋氣和，則商聲調。

translations.literal: When autumn's qi is harmonious, then the shang note is in tune.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn qi is balanced, shang rings true.

sentences.zh: 商亂則詖，其官壞也。

translations.literal: When shang is chaotic, then there is faction; its officials are ruined.
translations.idiomatic: When shang slips, factions form and the bureaucracy rots.

sentences.zh: 水音羽，三分商去一以生，其數四十八。

translations.literal: Water's timbre is yu; subtract one third from shang to engender it; its number is forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Water is yu, born by taking a third from shang, numbered forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 屬水者，以為最清，物之象也。

translations.literal: What belongs to water is that it is the clearest sound, image of things.
translations.idiomatic: Water sounds are the brightest in the pentad, like the myriad things in clarity.

sentences.zh: 冬氣和，則羽聲調。

translations.literal: When winter's qi is harmonious, then the yu note is in tune.
translations.idiomatic: When winter qi is balanced, yu rings true.

sentences.zh: 羽亂則危，其財匱也。

translations.literal: When yu is chaotic, then there is peril; its wealth is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When yu slips, danger looms and the treasury runs dry.

sentences.zh: 木音角，三分羽益一以生，其數六十四。

translations.literal: Wood's timbre is jue; add one third to yu to engender it; its number is sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Wood is jue, born by adding a third to yu, numbered sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 屬木者，以其清濁中，人之象也。

translations.literal: What belongs to wood is that it sits between clear and muddy, image of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wood timbre mediates bright and dark, like common folk between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 春氣和，則角聲調。

translations.literal: When spring's qi is harmonious, then the jue note is in tune.
translations.idiomatic: When spring qi is balanced, jue rings true.

sentences.zh: 角亂則憂，其人怨也。

translations.literal: When jue is chaotic, then there is worry; the people are resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When jue slips, anxiety spreads and the people grow bitter.

sentences.zh: 凡聲尊卑，取象五行，數多者濁，數少者清；

translations.literal: In general, for sound, high and low take image from the five phases: larger numbers are muddy, smaller numbers are clear;
translations.idiomatic: Pitch nobility mirrors the five phases: big tallies sound dull, small tallies bright—

sentences.zh: 大不過宮，細不過羽。

translations.literal: great does not surpass gong, fine does not surpass yu.
translations.idiomatic: the bass anchor never passes gong, the top shimmer never passes yu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，律中黃鐘，律之始也，長九寸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the pitch matches Yellow Bell—the beginning of the pipes—nine cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh month sits on Yellow Bell, the head of the twelve pipes, nine cùn long.

sentences.zh: 仲冬氣至，則其律應，所以宣養六氣九德也。

translations.literal: When mid-winter's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it propagates and nourishes the six qi and nine powers of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Midwinter's breath makes that pipe speak, broadcasting and feeding the six vapors and nine virtues.

sentences.zh: 班固三分損一，下生林鐘。

translations.literal: Ban Gu: subtracting one third downward begets Forest Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's cycle subtracts a third down to Forest Bell.

sentences.zh: 十二月，律中大呂，司馬遷未下生之律，長四寸二百四十三分寸之五十二，倍之為八寸二百四十三分寸之一百四。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the pitch matches Great Regulator—Sima Qian's pipe not yet generated downward—four cun and 52/243 cun, doubled to eight cun and 104/243 cun.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month takes Dàlǚ, Sima Qian's "not yet down-generated" length of four cùn fifty-two two-hundred-forty-thirds, doubled to eight cùn one hundred four parts.

sentences.zh: 季冬氣至，則其律應，所以助宣物也。

translations.literal: When late winter's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it assists in propagating the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Late winter's qi wakes Dàlǚ so it can push the year's growth outward.

sentences.zh: 三分益一，上生夷則；

translations.literal: Add one third upward to beget Yízé;
translations.idiomatic: Add a third upward and you reach Yízé;

sentences.zh: 京房三分損一，下生夷則。

translations.literal: Jing Fang: subtract one third downward to beget Yízé.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang instead subtracts a third downward to Yízé.

sentences.zh: 正月，律中太蔟，未上生之律，長八寸。

translations.literal: In the first month the pitch matches Tàicù—the upward-generated class from wèi—eight cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The first month keys to Tàicù, the "up from wèi" generated class, eight cùn long (the manuscript graph is the wei stem character, here read as the wèi-branch class).

sentences.zh: 孟春氣至，則其律應，所以贊陽出滯也。

translations.literal: When early spring's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it praises the yang and draws the pent-up forth.
translations.idiomatic: Early spring's qi hits Tàicù so the yang is praised and stagnation shaken loose.

sentences.zh: 三分損一，下生南呂。

translations.literal: Subtract one third downward to beget Southern Regulator.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract a third downward to reach Nánlǚ.

sentences.zh: 二月，律中夾鐘，酉下生之律，長三寸二千一百八十七分寸之一千六百三十一，倍之為七寸二千一百八十七分寸之一千七十五。

translations.literal: In the second month the pitch matches Jiázhōng—the downward-generated class from yǒu—three cun and 1631/2187 cun, doubled to seven cun and 1075/2187 cun.
translations.idiomatic: The second month takes Jiázhōng, the "down from yǒu" length of three cùn one thousand six hundred thirty-one two-thousand-one-hundred-eighty-sevenths, doubled to seven cùn one thousand seventy-five parts.

sentences.zh: 仲春氣至，則其律應，所以出四隙之細也。

translations.literal: When mid-spring's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it lets the fine detail slip through the four interstices.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-spring's qi answers Jiázhōng, threading subtlety through the four gaps of the year.

sentences.zh: 三分益一，上生無射；

translations.literal: Add one third upward to beget Wúyì;
translations.idiomatic: Add a third upward to reach Wúyì;

sentences.zh: 京房三分損一，下生無射。

translations.literal: Jing Fang: subtract one third downward to beget Wúyì.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang subtracts a third downward to Wúyì.

sentences.zh: 三月，律中姑洗，酉上生之律，長七寸九分寸之一。

translations.literal: In the third month the pitch matches Gǔxǐ—the upward-generated class from yǒu—seven cun and one ninth cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The third month keys to Gǔxǐ, the "up from yǒu" class, seven cùn and one-ninth cùn long.

sentences.zh: 季春氣至，則其律應，所以修絜百物，考神納賓也。

translations.literal: When late spring's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it rinses clean the hundred things and examines spirits and welcomes guests.
translations.idiomatic: Late spring's qi strikes Gǔxǐ to rinse offerings, draw spirits, and welcome guests.

sentences.zh: 三分損一，下生應鐘。

translations.literal: Subtract one third downward to beget Bell of Response.
translations.idiomatic: Drop a third downward to Yìngzhōng.

sentences.zh: 四月，律中中呂，亥下生之律，長三寸萬九千六百八十三分寸之六千四百八十七，倍之為六寸萬九千六百八十三分寸之萬二千九百七十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the pitch matches Zhònglǚ—the downward-generated class from hài—three cun and 6487/19683 cun, doubled to six cun and 12974/19683 cun.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth month takes Zhònglǚ, the "down from hài" length of three cùn six thousand four hundred eighty-seven nineteen-thousand-six-hundred-eighty-thirds, doubled to six cùn twelve thousand nine hundred seventy-four parts.

sentences.zh: 孟夏氣至，則其律應，所以宣中氣也。

translations.literal: When early summer's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it vents the central qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early summer's qi hits Zhònglǚ to vent the qi pooled at the year's hinge.

sentences.zh: 五月，律中蕤賓，亥上生之律，長六寸八十一分寸之二十六。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the pitch matches Ruibīn—the upward-generated class from hài—six cun and twenty-six eighty-firsts cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth month keys to Ruibīn, the "up from hài" pipe six cùn and twenty-six eighty-firsts long.

sentences.zh: 仲夏氣至，則其律應，所以安靜人神，獻酬交酢也。

translations.literal: When mid-summer's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it calms spirits and men and exchanges pledging cups.
translations.idiomatic: Midsummer's qi answers Ruibīn, the pitch of quiet worship and pledging cup after cup.

sentences.zh: 三分損一，下生大呂；

translations.literal: Subtract one third downward to beget Great Regulator;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract a third downward to Dàlǚ;

sentences.zh: 京房三分益一，上生大呂。

translations.literal: Jing Fang: add one third upward to beget Great Regulator.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang adds a third upward to Dàlǚ.

sentences.zh: 六月，律中林鐘，醜下生之律，長六寸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the pitch matches Forest Bell—the downward-generated class from chǒu—six cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth month takes Línzhōng, the "down from chǒu" pipe six cùn long.

sentences.zh: 季夏氣至，則其律應，所以和展百物，俾莫不任肅純恪也。

translations.literal: When late summer's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it harmonizes the hundred affairs so that none fail to rise in solemn purity.
translations.idiomatic: Late summer's qi strikes Línzhōng to harmonize every task in reverent care.

sentences.zh: 三分益一，上生太蔟。

translations.literal: Add one third upward to beget Tàicù.
translations.idiomatic: Add a third upward to Tàicù.

sentences.zh: 七月，律中夷則，醜上生之律，長五寸七百二十九分寸之四百五十一。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the pitch matches Yízé—the upward-generated class from chǒu—five cun and 451/729 cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh month keys to Yízé, the "up from chǒu" pipe five cùn four hundred fifty-one seven-hundred-twenty-ninths long.

sentences.zh: 孟秋氣至，則其律應，所以詠歌九則，平百姓而無貸也。

translations.literal: When early autumn's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it hymns the nine canons, levels the hundred surnames, and grants no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Early autumn's qi answers Yízé, the pipe that hymns the nine statutes, steadies the commoners, and brooks no slack (the phrase is "nine canons," not "nine virtues").

sentences.zh: 三分損一，下生夾鐘；

translations.literal: Subtract one third downward to beget Jiázhōng;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract a third downward to Jiázhōng;

sentences.zh: 京房三分益一，上生夾鐘。

translations.literal: Jing Fang: add one third upward to beget Jiázhōng.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang adds a third upward to Jiázhōng.

sentences.zh: 八月，律中南呂，卯下生之律，長五寸三分寸之一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the pitch matches Southern Regulator—the downward-generated class from mǎo—five cun and one third cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth month takes Nánlǚ, the "down from mǎo" pipe five cùn and one-third cùn long.

sentences.zh: 仲秋氣至，則其律應，所以贊陽秀也。

translations.literal: When mid-autumn's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it assists the flowering of the yang.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-autumn's qi answers Nánlǚ, coaxing the yang into full bloom.

sentences.zh: 三分益一，上生姑洗。

translations.literal: Add one third upward to beget Gǔxǐ.
translations.idiomatic: Add a third upward to Gǔxǐ.

sentences.zh: 九月，律中無射，卯上生之律，長四寸六千五百六十一分寸之六千五百二十四。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the pitch matches Wúyì—the upward-generated class from mǎo—four cun and 6524/6561 cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month keys to Wúyì, the "up from mǎo" pipe four cùn six thousand five hundred twenty-four six-thousand-five-hundred-sixty-firsts long.

sentences.zh: 季秋氣至，則其律應，所以宣佈哲人之令德，示人軌儀也。

translations.literal: When late autumn's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it proclaims the bright commands of the wise and displays models for conduct to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Late autumn's qi hits Wúyì to broadcast a sage's shining edicts and show the people their compass.

sentences.zh: 三分損一，下生中呂；

translations.literal: Subtract one third downward to beget Zhònglǚ;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract a third downward to Zhònglǚ;

sentences.zh: 京房三分益一，上生中呂。

translations.literal: Jing Fang: add one third upward to beget Zhònglǚ.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang adds a third upward to Zhònglǚ.

sentences.zh: 十月，律中應鐘，巳下生之律，長四寸二十七分寸之二十。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the pitch matches Bell of Response—the downward-generated class from sì—four cun and twenty twenty-sevenths cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth month takes Yìngzhōng, the "down from sì" pipe four cùn and twenty twenty-sevenths long.

sentences.zh: 孟冬氣至，則其律應，所以均利器用，俾應復也。

translations.literal: When early winter's qi arrives, then that pipe responds, whereby it evens sharp tools and responses so the cycle may begin again.
translations.idiomatic: Early winter's qi answers Yìngzhōng, evening tools and echoes so the circuit can close.

sentences.zh: 三分益一，上生蕤賓。

translations.literal: Add one third upward to beget Ruibīn.
translations.idiomatic: Add a third upward to Ruibīn.

sentences.zh: 淮南、京房、鄭玄諸儒言律曆，皆上下相生，至蕤賓又重上生大呂，長八寸二百四十三分寸之百四；

translations.literal: The Huainan masters, Jing Fang, Zhèng Xuán, and other scholars speak of pitch and calendar all as upper and lower mutual generation; at Ruibīn they again ascend to generate Great Regulator—eight cun and 104/243 cun long;
translations.idiomatic: Huainan, Jing Fang, Zhèng Xuán, and others all teach upper/lower thirds, but at Ruibīn they "ascend again" to Dàlǚ—eight cùn one hundred four two-hundred-forty-thirds—

sentences.zh: 夷則上生夾鐘，長七寸千一百八十七分寸之千七十五；

translations.literal: Yízé upward begets Jiázhōng—seven cun and 1075/1187 cun long;
translations.idiomatic: Yízé ascends to Jiázhōng at seven cùn one thousand seventy-five one-thousand-one-hundred-eighty-sevenths;

sentences.zh: 無射上生中呂，長六寸萬九千六百八十三分寸之萬二千九百七十四；

translations.literal: Wúyì upward begets Zhònglǚ—six cun and 12974/19683 cun long;
translations.idiomatic: Wúyì ascends to Zhònglǚ at six cùn twelve thousand nine hundred seventy-four nineteen-thousand-six-hundred-eighty-thirds;

sentences.zh: 此三品于司馬遷、班固所生之寸數及分皆倍焉，餘則並同。

translations.literal: These three grades double the cun numbers and fractional parts compared with what Sima Qian and Ban Gu engendered; the rest are all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Those three steps double the inch fractions Sima Qian and Ban Gu gave; every other length matches.

sentences.zh: 斯則泠州鳩所謂六間之道，揚沈伏，黜散越，假之為用者也。

translations.literal: This is what Lěng Zhōujiū called the way of the six interstices—floating what sinks too deep, pruning what scatters too wide—borrowing them for use.
translations.idiomatic: That is the six-interstice path Lěng Zhōujiū described: lift the sunken, trim the loose—borrowed for practical tuning.

sentences.zh: 變通相半，隨事之宜，贊助之法也。

translations.literal: Mutual change by halving follows the convenience of the affair, a method of assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Half-step swaps follow whatever the rite requires—they are aids, not the core thirds.

sentences.zh: 凡音聲之體，務在和均，益則加倍，損則減半，其於本音恆為無爽。

translations.literal: For the body of musical sound, the task is harmony and evenness: add and you double, subtract and you halve, relative to the root tone it always stays true.
translations.idiomatic: Sound wants balance: raise it and you double, lower it and you halve—against the fundamental it must never lie.

sentences.zh: 然則言一上一下者，相生之道；

translations.literal: Thus speaking of one ascent and one descent names the mutual-generation road;
translations.idiomatic: Talking of "one up, one down" names the true third-generation road—

sentences.zh: 言重上生者，吹候之用也。

translations.literal: speaking of repeated ascent names what blowing and listening employ.
translations.idiomatic: while "ascend again" names a listening trick for ash-tube tests.

sentences.zh: 於蕤賓重上生者，適會為用之數，故言律者因焉，非相生之正也。

translations.literal: At Ruibīn the repeated ascent hits a convenient number for application; therefore writers on pitch cite it, but it is not the orthodox rule of mutual generation.
translations.idiomatic: Ruibīn's double ascent lands on a handy tally for workshop use, so acousticians quote it, yet it is not canonical breeding.

sentences.zh: 楊子雲曰：「聲生於日，謂甲己為角，乙庚為商，丙辛為徵，丁壬為羽，戊癸為宮也。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong said: 'Sound is born from the days—meaning jiǎ and jǐ are jue, yǐ and gēng are shang, bǐng and xīn are zhi, dīng and rén are yu, wù and guǐ are gong.'
translations.idiomatic: Yáng Xióng said sound maps to the ten stems: jiǎ/jǐ as jue, yǐ/gēng as shang, bǐng/xīn as zhǐ, dīng/rén as yu, wù/guǐ as gong.

sentences.zh: 律生於辰，謂子為黃鐘，醜為大呂之屬也。

translations.literal: Pitch is born from the branches—meaning zǐ is Yellow Bell, chǒu is Great Regulator, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch maps to the twelve branches—zǐ as Yellow Bell, chǒu as Dàlǚ, and so down the ring—

sentences.zh: 聲以情質，質，正也。

translations.literal: Sound takes emotion as its substance; substance means correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Sound rides on feeling for its body, and "body" here means being true to type—

sentences.zh: 各以其行本情為正也。

translations.literal: each taking its element's native disposition as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: each degree staying loyal to the element that fathers it.

sentences.zh: 律以和聲，當以律管鐘均和其清濁之聲。

translations.literal: Pitch harmonizes sound; one should use pitch pipes and bells to even its clear and muddy voices.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes exist to tune sound: bronze tubes and matched bells must pull bright and dark voices into one line.

sentences.zh: 聲律相協而八音生。

translations.literal: When sound and pitch cooperate, the eight timbres arise.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch and timbre must agree before bronze, stone, silk, or bamboo can speak as the eight voices.

sentences.zh: 協，和也。

translations.literal: 'Cooperate' means 'harmonize.'
translations.idiomatic: Here xie simply means "bring into tune."

sentences.zh: 」宮、商、角、徵、羽，謂之五聲。

translations.literal: Gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu are called the five sounds.
translations.idiomatic: The five named scale degrees are gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu.

sentences.zh: 金、石、匏、革、絲、竹、土、木，謂之八音。

translations.literal: Metal, stone, gourd, hide, silk, bamboo, earth, and wood are called the eight timbres.
translations.idiomatic: The eight material sources are metal, stone, gourd, leather, silk, bamboo, clay, and wood.

sentences.zh: 聲和音諧，是謂五樂。

translations.literal: When sound and timbre are both harmonious, this is called the five musics.
translations.idiomatic: That mutual tuning of voice and material is what the canon calls the "five musics."

sentences.zh: 夫陰陽和則景至，律氣應則灰除。

translations.literal: When yin and yang are in harmony the shadow arrives true; when the pipe's qi responds the ash is cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: Solstitial harmony shows in the gnomon; the monthly pipe's breath shows when the ash flies.

sentences.zh: 是故天子常以冬夏至日御前殿，合八能之士，陳八音，聽樂均，度晷景，候鐘律，權土灰，效陰陽，冬至陽氣應則灰除，是故樂均清，景長極，黃鐘通，土灰輕而衡仰。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven regularly on the winter- and summer-solstice days sits in the forward hall, gathers masters of the eight skills, arrays the eight timbres, listens for even tuning, measures the gnomon's shadow, tests bells and pitch pipes, weighs earth and ash, and mirrors yin and yang; at the winter solstice, when yang qi responds, the ash clears—hence the tuning is clear, the shadow reaches its maximum length, Yellow Bell speaks, the earth-ash is light, and the balance arm rises.
translations.idiomatic: On both solstices the king convenes the eight experts in the forward hall: they sound the eight colors of instrument, check ensemble balance, read the sundial, listen to bells and pipes, weigh thermoscopic ash, and read yin against yang—at midwinter yang answers so the ash flies, the pitch turns bright, the shadow stretches to its yearly maximum, Yellow Bell opens, the ash pan lightens, and the steelyard's beam lifts.

sentences.zh: 夏至陰氣應則樂均濁，景短極，蕤賓通，土灰重而衡低。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice, when yin qi responds, the tuning turns muddy, the shadow reaches its minimum length, Ruibīn speaks, the earth-ash is heavy, and the balance arm sinks.
translations.idiomatic: At midsummer yin answers: the band slides toward duller color, the gnomon throws its shortest mark, Ruibīn opens, the ash tray weighs heavy, and the balance sinks.

sentences.zh: 進退於先後五日之中，八能各以候狀聞，太史令封上。

translations.literal: Within the five days before and after, each of the eight experts reports what he observed; the Grand Astrologer seals and submits them.
translations.idiomatic: Across the ten-day solstice window each master files his reading, and the Grand Astrologer forwards the sealed bundle.

sentences.zh: 效則和，否則占。

translations.literal: If the response matches, there is harmony; if not, it becomes an omen.
translations.idiomatic: Agreement means peace; mismatch becomes divination.

sentences.zh: 候氣之法，為室三重，戶閉，塗釁周密，布緹幔。

translations.literal: The method for awaiting qi builds a chamber of three nested layers, doors shut, seams sealed with paste, and crimson curtains hung.
translations.idiomatic: Breath-testing needs a triple room: sealed doors, pasted joints, red curtains drawn.

sentences.zh: 室中以木為案，每律各一，內房中外高，從其方位，加律其上，以葭莩灰抑其內端，案曆而候之：氣至者灰去；

translations.literal: Inside, wooden tables are set, one for each pitch pipe, inner low and outer high according to their direction; the pipe is placed on top, reed-ash is pressed at its inner end, and one waits by the calendar: when qi arrives the ash flies away.
translations.idiomatic: Inside stand twelve tables, each bearing a pipe oriented to its compass point; pack reed ash in the bore, watch the calendar, and when the month's breath hits, the ash puffs out.

sentences.zh: 其為氣所動者，其灰散；

translations.literal: Where qi stirs it, the ash scatters.
translations.idiomatic: A true cosmic puff scatters the grains.

sentences.zh: 人及風所動者，其灰聚。

translations.literal: Where men or wind stir it, the ash clumps.
translations.idiomatic: Human breath or a draft merely clumps the ash.

sentences.zh: 殿中候用玉律十二，惟二至乃候。

translations.literal: In the palace hall twelve jade pitch pipes are used for listening; only the two solstices are tested.
translations.idiomatic: The throne hall keeps twelve jade pipes for the two solstices alone.

sentences.zh: 靈台用竹律。

translations.literal: The Spirit Terrace uses bamboo pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The observatory relies on bamboo tubes instead.

sentences.zh: 楊泉記云：「取弘農宜陽縣金門山竹為管，河內葭莩為灰。

translations.literal: Yang Quan's record says: 'They took bamboo from the Golden Gate mountains of Yiyang in Hongnong and reed fluff from Henei for the ash.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Quan notes bamboo cut on Mount Jīnmén in Yiyang and reed ash from Henei.

sentences.zh: 」或云以律著室中，隨十二辰埋之，上與地平，以竹莩灰實律中，以羅縠覆律呂，氣至吹灰動縠。

translations.literal: Another account says the pipes were set in the chamber, buried level with the ground along the twelve branches, filled to the inner lip with bamboo-membrane ash, and covered with gauze; when qi arrived it blew the ash and stirred the gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Another rite buries the twelve tubes flush with the floor by the twelve branches, fills them with membrane ash, veils them in gauze, and waits for the puff that lifts the cloth.

sentences.zh: 小動為和，大動，君弱臣強；

translations.literal: A slight motion means harmony; a great motion means the ruler is weak and ministers strong.
translations.idiomatic: A tremble means balance; a gale hints ministers overpowering the throne.

sentences.zh: 不動，君嚴暴之應也。

translations.literal: No motion means the portent of a harsh, violent ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Dead stillness foretells a cruel king.

sentences.zh: 起度之正，《漢志》言之詳矣。

translations.literal: The correct foundation of measurement, the 'Book of Han' monograph explains in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu already spelled out the true foot-rule in the Han treatise.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始九年，中書監荀勖校太樂，八音不和，始知後漢至魏，尺長於古四分有餘。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taishi ninth year, Palace Secretariat Supervisor Xun Xi corrected the Grand Music; the eight timbres would not harmonize, and only then was it learned that from Later Han through Wei the foot had grown more than four fen longer than antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Wudi's Taishi 9 Xun Xi retuned the court band and found Eastern Han and Wei had stretched the foot more than four fēn past the old standard.

sentences.zh: 勖乃部著作郎劉恭依《周禮》制尺，所謂古尺也。

translations.literal: Xun Xi therefore assigned Editorial Director Liu Gong to fashion a foot after the 'Rites of Zhou'—what men call the ancient foot.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Gong to cut the "Zhou foot" that antiquarians prize.

sentences.zh: 依古尺更鑄銅律呂，以調聲韻。

translations.literal: According to that ancient foot he recast the bronze pitch pipes to regulate tones.
translations.idiomatic: From that measure he cast fresh bronze pipes.

sentences.zh: 以尺量古器，與本銘尺寸無差。

translations.literal: Measuring old vessels with the foot matched every inscription without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Every heirloom bronze measured true to its own inscription.

sentences.zh: 又，汲郡盜發六國時魏襄王塚，得古周時玉律及鐘、磬，與新律聲韻闇同。

translations.literal: Moreover, when tomb robbers opened King Xiang of Wei's Warring States grave in Ji commandery, they recovered Zhou jade pitch pipes and bells and chimes whose timbre matched the new pipes in the dark.
translations.idiomatic: Plunderers who cracked King Xiang's tomb at Ji turned up Zhou jade pipes and bells that sang in tune with Xun Xi's new set.

sentences.zh: 于時郡國或得漢時故鐘，吹律命之皆應。

translations.literal: At that time commanderies that recovered Han-era bells found they all answered when blown to the pipes.
translations.idiomatic: When stray Han bells surfaced in the provinces, each spoke correctly to the new tubes.

sentences.zh: 勖銘其尺曰：「晉泰始十年，中書考古器，揆校今尺，長四分半。

translations.literal: Xun Xi inscribed his foot: 'In Jin Taishi ten the Palace Secretariat examined antiquities and compared them with the present foot, which is four and a half fen too long.'
translations.idiomatic: He stamped the ruler with a Taishi-10 colophon comparing it to the bloated contemporary foot.

sentences.zh: 所校古法有七品：一曰姑洗玉律，二曰小呂玉律，三曰西京銅望臬，四曰金錯望臬，五曰銅斛，六曰古錢，七曰建武銅尺。

translations.literal: The corrected ancient methods fell into seven grades: first, the Gǔxǐ jade pipe; second, the lesser lǚ jade pipe; third, the Western capital bronze gnomon; fourth, the gold-inlaid gnomon; fifth, the bronze hu measure; sixth, old coinage; seventh, the Jianwu bronze foot.
translations.idiomatic: Seven relics anchored the proof: Gǔxǐ and lesser lǚ jade pipes, two Han gnomons, the standard hu, old cash, and the Jianwu foot.

sentences.zh: 姑洗微強，西京望臬微弱，其餘與此尺同。

translations.literal: Gǔxǐ was slightly sharp, the Western capital gnomon slightly dull; the rest matched this foot exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gǔxǐ read a hair bright and the Han gnomon a hair flat—everything else lined up.

sentences.zh: 」銘八十二字。

translations.literal: The inscription ran eighty-two characters.
translations.idiomatic: The colophon holds eighty-two graphs.

sentences.zh: 此尺者勖新尺也，今尺者杜夔尺也。

translations.literal: This foot is Xun Xi's new foot; the present foot is Du Kui's foot.
translations.idiomatic: That ruler is Xun Xi's new measure; the older court foot is Du Kui's.

sentences.zh: 荀勖造新鐘律，與古器諧韻，時人稱其精密，惟散騎侍郎陳留阮咸譏其聲高，聲高則悲，非興國之音，亡國之音。

translations.literal: Xun Xi cast new bells and pipes to match antiquity; people praised their fineness, but Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Ruǎn Xiǎn of Chenliu mocked their high pitch—'High pitch is mournful, not the sound that raises a state; it is the sound of perishing states.'
translations.idiomatic: The court admired Xun's crisp bells, yet Ruǎn Xiǎn sneered that they rang sharp—and sharp music, he said, is the whine of dying dynasties.

sentences.zh: 亡國之音哀以思，其人困。

translations.literal: The music of a perishing state is mournful and brooding; its people are distressed.
translations.idiomatic: A dying state's airs are sad and thoughtful; its people are cornered.

sentences.zh: 今聲不合雅，懼非德正至和之音，必古今尺有長短所致也。

translations.literal: Today's sounds do not match ya refinement; I fear they are not the utterly virtuous, perfectly harmonious note—this must come from ancient and modern feet being long or short.
translations.idiomatic: Ruǎn adds that the new pitch feels un-ya: unless the foot itself has drifted, you cannot get the morally "level" tone the classics demand.

sentences.zh: 會咸病卒，武帝以勖律與周漢器合，故施用之。

translations.literal: When Ruǎn Xiǎn soon died of illness, Emperor Wu, because Xun Xi's pipes matched Zhou and Han vessels, therefore put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Ruǎn died young; Wudi still adopted Xun's law because it matched Zhou and Han bronze.

sentences.zh: 後始平掘地得古銅尺，歲久欲腐，不知所出何代，果長勖尺四分，時人服咸之妙，而莫能厝意焉。

translations.literal: Later, at Shǐpíng they dug up an ancient bronze foot from the earth; after long years it was almost rotted away and no one knew which dynasty had left it, yet it proved four fen longer than Xun Xi's foot—then men marveled at Ruǎn's insight though none could settle the dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Later diggers at Shǐpíng unearthed a corroded old ruler four fēn longer than Xun's—vindicating Ruǎn's ear while the debate raged on.

sentences.zh: 史臣案：「勖於千載之外，推百代之法，度數既宜，聲韻又契，可謂切密，信而有徵也。

translations.literal: The historiographers remark: 'Xun Xi, a thousand years later, reconstructed the methods of a hundred generations; his numbers fit and his timbres answered—how precise, how trustworthy.'
translations.idiomatic: The annalists still call Xun Xi's reconstruction razor-sharp and well attested.

sentences.zh: 而時人寡識，據無聞之一尺，忽周漢之兩器，雷同臧否，何其謬哉！

translations.literal: Yet people of the time were shallow in knowledge: they clung to one obscure foot, neglected two Zhou and Han instruments, and echoed one another in praise or blame—how absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Yet shallow contemporaries waved one stray ruler, ignored two Han standards, and parroted the same verdict—sheer folly.

sentences.zh: 《世說》稱「有田父于野地中得周時玉尺，便是天下正尺，荀勖試以校己所治金石絲竹，皆短校一米」。

translations.literal: The 'New Tales' records that 'a farmer found a Zhou jade foot-rule in the wild; that was the true foot of the realm, and when Xun Xi tried it against his metal, stone, silk, and bamboo, everything was short by almost a meter.'
translations.idiomatic: The Shishuo adds a farmer's Zhou jade ruler that made Xun's entire orchestra look a meter short.

sentences.zh: 又，漢章帝時，零陵文學史奚景於泠道舜祠下得玉律，度以為尺，相傳謂之漢官尺。

translations.literal: Again, in Han Emperor Zhang's time the Lingling clerk Xi Jing found a jade pitch pipe in the Shun shrine at Lengdao and took its length as a foot—tradition calls it the Han official foot.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhangdi's Lingling clerk Xi Jing also cut a "Han office foot" from Shun's jade pipe.

sentences.zh: 以校荀勖尺，勖尺短四分；

translations.literal: Compared against Xun Xi's foot, Xun's foot is four fen short.
translations.idiomatic: Stacked against the Han office ruler, Xun's foot comes up four fēn short.

sentences.zh: 漢官、始平兩尺，長短度同。

translations.literal: The Han official and Shǐpíng feet agree in length.
translations.idiomatic: The Han office foot and the Shǐpíng find match each other.

sentences.zh: 又，杜夔所用調律尺，比勖新尺，得一尺四分七厘。

translations.literal: Again, the foot-rule Du Kui used to tune pipes, compared with Xun Xi's new foot, yields one chi four fen seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui's tuning foot against Xun's new foot works out to one chǐ four fēn seven lí.

sentences.zh: 魏景元四年，劉徽注《九章》云：王莽時劉歆斛尺弱於今尺四分五厘，比魏尺其斛深九寸五分厘；

translations.literal: In Wei Jingyuan fourth year, Liu Hui annotated the 'Nine Chapters': 'Wang Mang's Liu Xin hu foot is weaker than today's foot by four fen five li; compared with the Wei foot its hu is nine cun five fen deep.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jingyuan 4: Liu Hui notes Wang Mang's hú foot falls four fēn five lí short of the Jin foot, leaving the hú nine cùn five fēn deep against Wei measure.

sentences.zh: 即荀勖所謂今尺長四分半是也。

translations.literal: This is precisely what Xun Xi meant by saying the present foot is four and a half fen too long.
translations.idiomatic: That is exactly Xun Xi's complaint that the current foot overshoots by four and a half fēn.

sentences.zh: 元帝后，江東所用尺，比荀勖尺一尺六分二厘。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yuan, the foot used east of the Yangzi was one chi six fen two li longer than Xun Xi's foot.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Yuan Jiangnan adopted a foot one chǐ six fēn two lí longer than Xun's.

sentences.zh: 趙劉曜光初四年鑄渾儀，八年鑄土圭，其尺比荀勖尺一尺五分。

translations.literal: In Zhao Liu Yao's Guangchu fourth year they cast an armillary; in the eighth year they cast a earth gnomon; its foot was one chi five fen longer than Xun Xi's foot.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's Zhao court cast instruments with a foot one chǐ five fēn longer than Xun's.

sentences.zh: 荀勖新尺惟以調音律，至於人間未甚流布，故江左及劉曜儀錶，並與魏尺略相依准。

translations.literal: Xun Xi's new foot was used only to tune pitch pipes; it did not circulate widely among the people, so the instruments and gnomons of the Jiangzuo courts and of Liu Yao still largely followed the Wei foot.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xun's foot stayed inside the music bureau, southern instruments and Liu Yao's observatory still hewed to the longer Wei foot.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》：「栗氏為量，鬴深尺，內方尺而圓其外，其實一鬴。

translations.literal: The 'Rites of Zhou' says: 'The office of the well-spring makes measures; the fu is one chi deep inside a square chi, rounded on the outside, and its capacity is one fu.'
translations.idiomatic: The "Rites of Zhou" puts the foundry officer in charge of the standard fu: a square foot inside, walls rounded outside, one foot deep, one fu in volume.

sentences.zh: 其臀一寸，其實一豆。

translations.literal: Its base extends one cun; its capacity is one dou.
translations.idiomatic: The pedestal adds one cùn; that compartment holds one dǒu.

sentences.zh: 其耳三寸，其實一升。

translations.literal: Its ears span three cun; their capacity is one sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The lifting ears add three cùn and hold one shēng.

sentences.zh: 重一鈞，其聲中黃鐘。

translations.literal: It weighs one jun and its tone matches Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: The whole piece weighs one jūn and rings Yellow Bell true.

sentences.zh: 概而不稅。

translations.literal: It is struck level and not taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Scrape the strike flat without shaving extra duty into the measure.

sentences.zh: 其銘曰：'時文思索，允臻其極。

translations.literal: Its inscription reads: 'Our cultured king pondered deeply and truly reached the utmost.'
translations.idiomatic: The lid proclaims that thoughtful kings hit the utmost mark.

sentences.zh: 嘉量既成，以觀四國。

translations.literal: Once the commendable measure was finished, he showed it to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the honest measure was cast, he displayed it to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 永啟厥後，茲器維則。

translations.literal: 'Forever open your heirs—let this vessel be their pattern.'
translations.idiomatic: "May your heirs take this vessel as their pattern forever."

sentences.zh: '」《春秋左氏傳》曰：「齊舊四量，豆、區、釜、鐘。

translations.literal: The 'Zuo Commentary' says: 'Qi formerly had four measures—dou, ōu, fǔ, and zhōng.'
translations.idiomatic: The "Zuo" adds that old Qi used four jars—dòu, ōu, fǔ, and the zhōng.

sentences.zh: 四升曰豆，各自其四，以登於釜。

translations.literal: Four shēng make a dòu; each step multiplies by four to mount the fǔ.
translations.idiomatic: Four shēng fill a dòu; each tier climbs by fours toward the fǔ.

sentences.zh: 」四豆為區，區鬥六升也。

translations.literal: Four dòu make an ōu; an ōu holds six shēng.
translations.idiomatic: Four dòu fill an ōu, and that ōu levels out at six shēng.

sentences.zh: 四區為釜，六斗四升也。

translations.literal: Four ōu make a fǔ—six dǒu four shēng.
translations.idiomatic: Four ōu make a fǔ, which is six dǒu and four shēng.

sentences.zh: 釜十則鐘，六十四斗也。

translations.literal: Ten fǔ make a zhōng—sixty-four dǒu.
translations.idiomatic: Ten fǔ make a zhōng, totaling sixty-four dǒu.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄以為釜方尺，積千寸，比《九章粟米法》少二升八十一分升之二十二。

translations.literal: Zhèng Xuán held that the fǔ was a square chi in cross-section, stacking to one thousand cun, which compared with the 'Nine Chapters' millet method shorted two sheng and twenty-two eighty-firsts of a sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhèng Xuán's cubic-foot fǔ tallies a thousand cubic cun—two shēng and twenty-two eighty-firsts shy of the "Nine Chapters" grain reckoning.

sentences.zh: 以算術考之，古斛之積凡一千五百六十二寸半，方尺而圓其外，減傍一厘八毫，其徑一尺四寸一分四毫七秒二忽有奇，而深尺，即古斛之制也。

translations.literal: Checked by arithmetic, the old hu's volume totals one thousand five hundred sixty-two and a half cubic cun; square on the outside with a circle inscribed, shaving one li eight hao from the side, the diameter is one chi four cun one fen four hao seven seconds two hu with remainder, and the depth one chi—this is the old hu's form.
translations.idiomatic: Math shows the classic hu at one thousand five hundred sixty-two and a half cubic cun: a square with a circle struck outside, nibbling one lí eight háo from the flank, yields diameter one chǐ four cùn one fēn four háo seven miǎo two hū with remainder for a depth of one chǐ—the canonical hu.

sentences.zh: 《九章商功法》程粟一斛，積二千七百寸；

translations.literal: The 'Nine Chapters' excavation method sets one hu of hulled millet at two thousand seven hundred cubic cun;
translations.idiomatic: The "Nine Chapters" labor chapter sets one hú of grain at two thousand seven hundred cubic cun;

sentences.zh: 米一斛，積一千六百二十七寸；

translations.literal: one hu of rice at one thousand six hundred twenty-seven cubic cun;
translations.idiomatic: one hú of polished rice at one thousand six hundred twenty-seven;

sentences.zh: 菽荅麻麥一斛，積二千四百三十寸。

translations.literal: one hu of beans, peas, hemp, or wheat at two thousand four hundred thirty cubic cun.
translations.idiomatic: and one hú of beans, peas, hemp, or wheat at two thousand four hundred thirty.

sentences.zh: 此據精粗為率，使價齊，而不等其器之積寸也。

translations.literal: This follows fine versus coarse ratios to equalize price without making every vessel's cubic cun identical.
translations.idiomatic: Those figures weight coarse against fine so market prices line up even when the jars differ.

sentences.zh: 以米斛為正，則同於《漢志》。

translations.literal: Taking the rice hu as standard matches the 'Book of Han' monograph.
translations.idiomatic: Using the rice hú as baseline lands on the same number Ban Gu gave.

sentences.zh: 魏陳留王景元四年，劉徽注《九章商功》曰：「當今大司農斛，圓徑一尺三寸五分五厘，深一尺，積一千四百四十一寸十分寸之三。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Chenliu's Jingyuan fourth year, Liu Hui annotated the 'Nine Chapters' excavation chapter: 'The present Minister of Agriculture hu has diameter one chi three cun five fen five li, depth one chi, capacity one thousand four hundred forty-one and three-tenths cubic cun.'
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Jingyuan 4 Liu Hui glossed the "Nine Chapters": the minister's hu measures one chǐ three cùn five fēn five lí across, one chǐ deep, one thousand four hundred forty-one and three-tenths cubic cun inside.

sentences.zh: 王莽銅斛，於今尺為深九寸五分五厘，徑一尺三寸六分八厘七毫。

translations.literal: Wang Mang's bronze hu, measured by today's foot, is nine cun five fen five li deep and one chi three cun six fen eight li seven hao in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's bronze hú, converted to Jin feet, is nine cùn five fēn five lí deep and one chǐ three cùn six fēn eight lí seven háo across.

sentences.zh: 以徽術計之，於今斛為容九斗七升四合有奇。

translations.literal: Computed by Hui's method, in today's hu it holds nine dǒu seven shēng four gě with remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui's π method makes the same vessel hold nine dǒu seven shēng four gě plus a trace.

sentences.zh: 」魏斛大而尺長，王莽斛小而尺短也。

translations.literal: Thus the Wei hu is large and the foot long; Wang Mang's hu is small and the foot short.'
translations.idiomatic: So the Wei measure runs large with a long foot, while Wang Mang's runs small with a short foot.

sentences.zh: 衡權者，衡，平也；

translations.literal: For weights and steelyards: 'heng' means level;
translations.idiomatic: Weights and balances: héng means even;

sentences.zh: 權，重也。

translations.literal: 'quan' means heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: quán names the counterweight.

sentences.zh: 衡所以任權而均物，平輕重也。

translations.literal: The steelyard exists to bear the counterweight and even things, leveling light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The beam carries the weight and evens the load—true light against true heavy.

sentences.zh: 古有黍、壘、錘、錙、鐶、鈞、鋝、鎰之目，歷代參差。

translations.literal: Antiquity had the categories shǔ, lěi, chuí, zī, huán, jūn, zhuó, and yì, shifting across dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Older metrologies listed shǔ, lěi, chuí, zī, huán, jūn, zhuó, and yì—each dynasty tweaked the names.

sentences.zh: 《漢志》言衡權名理甚備，自後變更，其詳未聞。

translations.literal: The 'Book of Han' monograph on heng and quan is very thorough; later changes are not recorded in detail here.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's treatise already explains weights exhaustively; later tweaks are not copied in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 元康中，裴頠以為醫方人命之急，而稱兩不與古同，為害特重，宜因此改治權衡，不見省。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era, Pei Yi held that medical prescriptions concern men's lives urgently, yet their liang did not match antiquity, doing singular harm; he therefore asked to reform weights and balances on that account, but the proposal was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang Pei Yì pleaded to realign medical weights—people's lives hung on every liǎng—but the court tabled his memo.

sentences.zh: 趙石勒十八年七月，造建德殿，得圓石，狀如水碓，銘曰：「律權石，重四鈞，同律度量衡。

translations.literal: In Zhao Shi Le's eighteenth year, seventh month, while building the Jiande Hall, they obtained a round stone shaped like a water pestle, inscribed: 'Pitch counterweight stone, weighing four jūn—unifies pitch, measure, and balance.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's builders turned up a round "law stone" counterweight marked four jūn, claiming it harmonized pitch, length, and weight.

sentences.zh: 有辛氏造。

translations.literal: It says the Xin family cast it.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription credits the Xin house.

sentences.zh: 」續咸議，是王莽時物。

translations.literal: Xù Xián argued that it was an object from Wang Mang's time.
translations.idiomatic: Xù Xián read the stone as another Wang Mang relic.
